text:
DOCUMENT: Comparison of 1st and 2nd edition of ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Cross-Market Manipulation and Physical Withholding
ID: 61
CONTENT:
Cross-market manipulation involves trading on one market to improperly position prices of related wholesale energy products on another market. This includes trading in underlying products of derivatives to distort derivative contract prices. Legitimate arbitrage transactions exploiting price differences across locations do not constitute manipulation.

Physical withholding occurs when market participants artificially cause prices at levels not justified by supply and demand forces, including actual availability of production, storage, or transportation capacity. Examples include not offering available production capacity without justification to shift market prices higher, or misusing infrastructure and transmission capacities resulting in abnormally high prices.

text:
DOCUMENT: Comparison of 1st and 2nd edition of ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Fictitious Devices and Deceptive Transactions
ID: 62
CONTENT:
Dissemination of false or misleading market information through media or internet with intention to move wholesale energy product prices favorably to the disseminator's position or planned transactions is prohibited. This practice is known as 'scalping' in some jurisdictions.

Pump and dump involves taking a long position in a wholesale energy product, undertaking further buying activity and/or disseminating misleading positive information to increase prices, attracting other market participants to purchase before the manipulator sells at inflated prices.

Circular trading executes sell orders with knowledge that offsetting buy orders are placed simultaneously, excluding competition and constituting illegal activity.

Pre-arranged trading involves two commodity dealers trading at previously agreed prices designed to exclude other dealers or gain tax advantages. The Agency considers certain practices like crossing/pre-arranged trades as accepted market practices not constituting manipulation if undertaken according to trading venue rules.

text:
DOCUMENT: Comparison of 1st and 2nd edition of ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Dissemination of False and Misleading Information
ID: 63
CONTENT:
Market manipulation through dissemination of false and misleading information occurs without necessarily accompanying transactions. This includes creating misleading impressions by failing to properly disclose price-sensitive information that should be disclosed, such as inside information under Regulation definitions.

Spreading false/misleading information through media involves posting via internet or issuing press releases containing false or misleading statements about wholesale energy products admitted to trading on organized markets. The person spreading information knows or ought to know it is false or misleading and disseminates it to create false impressions. Spreading through officially recognized information channels is particularly serious as market participants must rely on such official channels.

Other behavior designed to spread false/misleading information covers conduct giving false impressions through means other than media, such as moving physical commodity stocks to create misleading impressions about supply, demand, or deliverables into commodity futures contracts.

text:
DOCUMENT: Comparison of 1st and 2nd edition of ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Market Manipulation Guidance and Conclusions
ID: 64
CONTENT:
Examples of practices constituting market manipulation are inspired by NRAs' experiences and financial market authorities' experiences, with whom ACER and NRAs cooperate in REMIT application. These examples indicate possible signals of market manipulation in wholesale energy markets according to REMIT, applicable until more experience is gained.

Market participants' behavior must be coherent with technical and economic constraints complying with competition law, especially concerning market power exercise. Cooperation between the Agency, NRAs, and competition authorities is essential. The Agency will constantly review its Guidance on market manipulation and publish revised non-binding Guidance when appropriate.

text:
DOCUMENT: Comparison of 1st and 2nd edition of ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Inside Information Disclosure Obligations Under REMIT
ID: 65
CONTENT:
Article 4(1) of REMIT obliges market participants to publicly disclose inside information in effective and timely manner regarding business or facilities which the market participant, its parent undertaking, or related undertaking owns, controls, or for whose operational matters the market participant is responsible, either wholly or partially.

The disclosure obligation applies to market participants as defined in Article 2(7) of REMIT. The obligation extends to inside information of parent undertakings or related undertakings, and to inside information regarding business or facilities the market participant controls or for whose operational matters it is responsible.

Article 4(3) extends disclosure obligations to persons employed by or acting on behalf of market participants receiving inside information in normal course of employment, profession, or duties. Such persons must ensure simultaneous, complete, and effective disclosure. However, this does not apply if the person has a duty of confidentiality from law, regulation, articles of association, or contracts. No such exception applies to market participants regarding parent or related undertakings under Article 4(1).

text:
DOCUMENT: Comparison of 1st and 2nd edition of ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Effective Public Disclosure of Inside Information
ID: 66
CONTENT:
Inside information should be disclosed ensuring capability of dissemination to as wide a public as possible. The Agency considers disclosure through platforms as most effective.

For effective and timely disclosure, the Agency currently recommends a dual approach: If platforms for inside information disclosure exist, operated by Transmission System Operators (TSOs) like RTE-UFE transparency initiative or energy exchanges like Nord Pool Spot and EEX Transparency platform, in accordance with Regulations (EC) No 714/2009 and (EC) No 715/2009 including guidelines and network codes, market participants with inside information should use such disclosure mechanisms unless otherwise specified in relevant rules, regulations, or by competent NRA.

According to Article 4(1) of REMIT, publication of inside information including in aggregated form in accordance with Regulation (EC) No 714/2009 or (EC) No 715/2009, or guidelines and network codes adopted pursuant to those Regulations, constitutes simultaneous, complete, and effective public disclosure. Transparency platforms should be used for further inside information disclosure, making simultaneous publication on market participant websites unnecessary if transparency platforms disclose information timely.

text:
DOCUMENT: Comparison of 1st and 2nd edition of ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Transparency Platforms and Inside Information Disclosure Requirements
ID: 67
CONTENT:
Transparency platforms lead to easier accessible information for all market participants. If adequate transparency platforms do not exist or simultaneously to publication through a platform, market participants may publish inside information on their own website for an interim period. Disclosure must enhance transparency across the EU and not distort information dissemination. Inside information shall be disclosed free of charge, in a nondiscriminatory, user-friendly and quantifiable manner. Information should be published in the official language(s) of the relevant Member State and in English or in English only. Publications must contain: the caption 'Publication according to Article 4(1) of REMIT / UMM – Urgent Market Message', a subject heading summarizing main content, the name and contact information of the market participant, if applicable the name and location of the respective asset, if applicable the balancing area or market area concerned, and the time and date of the relevant occurrence including estimated duration of outages. According to Article 2(7) of REMIT, TSOs are market participants themselves.

text:
DOCUMENT: Comparison of 1st and 2nd edition of ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Publication Content Requirements and Standards
ID: 68
CONTENT:
Publications must include the time and date of publication, if applicable the reasons for unavailability of generation units, consumption units or parts of electricity or gas grid, and if applicable a history of prior publications regarding the same event. Each publication should be as short as reasonably possible and usually not exceed 10 to 20 lines. Publications should not include statements by company executives, advertisements or irrelevant information. The Agency discourages the use of disclaimers; if used, they should be clearly separated from the main body. If a prognosis is required regarding duration of outage, it must be based on all available data and prepared with reasonable effort. If a prognosis changes, the publication must be updated accordingly. Incomplete or incorrect disclosure would be considered non-effective disclosure and breach of Article 4(1) of REMIT.

text:
DOCUMENT: Comparison of 1st and 2nd edition of ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: IT Standards and Regulated Information Service (RIS) Requirements
ID: 69
CONTENT:
Platforms must fulfill RIS requirements: have adequate policies and arrangements to make public inside information as close to real time as technically possible on reasonable commercial basis; efficiently and consistently disseminate inside information ensuring fast access on non-discriminatory basis in format facilitating consolidation with similar data; ensure high availability consistent with market expectations; operate and maintain effective administrative arrangements preventing conflicts of interest with market participants; have sound security mechanisms guaranteeing security of information transfer, minimizing data corruption risk and unauthorized access, preventing information leakage before publication; maintain adequate resources and backup facilities avoiding temporary technical problems; define emergency procedures for platform outages; report inside information received to the Agency and NRAs as non-aggregated individual data once REMIT implementing acts apply; keep historic inside information available for at least 2 years.

text:
DOCUMENT: Comparison of 1st and 2nd edition of ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Website Disclosure and Social Media Guidelines
ID: 70
CONTENT:
Market participants disclosing inside information on their own website as fallback or simultaneously to platform disclosure shall make information available through web feeds in format facilitating consolidation with similar data. Social media shall only be used as additional sources not replacing website publications. Historic inside information should remain available on market participants' website for at least 2 years if not retained by inside information platform, allowing other market participants to learn best practice disclosure and assess previous incidents. Market participants are not responsible for temporary technical problems of transparency platforms fulfilling RIS requirements. If information was transmitted to platform in time, market participant should not be charged with breaching disclosure obligation. If technical problems persist, market participants must use other platforms or their own website. Although delayed disclosure due to technical problems does not imply breach, market participant cannot trade based on that information until available to market.

text:
DOCUMENT: Comparison of 1st and 2nd edition of ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Timely Public Disclosure of Inside Information
ID: 71
CONTENT:
If inside information must be published in accordance with Regulations (EC) No 714/2009 and (EC) No 715/2009, including guidelines and network codes, the delay in publishing under these rules including in aggregated form is considered simultaneous, complete and effective public disclosure under Article 4(4) of REMIT. However, publication in aggregated form does not necessarily constitute timely disclosure; inside information must be published before prohibition of insider trading ceases to apply. If inside information does not require publication under Regulations (EC) No 714/2009 and (EC) No 715/2009, there is no reason for different reasonable timeframe; such information must normally be published within one hour unless otherwise specified. In any case, inside information must be published before prohibition of insider trading ceases to apply. Market participants should develop clear compliance plans toward real time or close to real time disclosure beyond existing Third Package transparency obligations.

text:
DOCUMENT: Comparison of 1st and 2nd edition of ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Exemptions and Reporting Requirements for Inside Information
ID: 72
CONTENT:
Article 3(4)(b) and Article 4(2) of REMIT provide exemptions from timely publication obligation and prohibition to trade before publication in specified cases. However, relevant information must be reported to the Agency and relevant NRA without delay. The Agency has developed a standard notification format based on financial markets experience and recommends adoption by all NRAs. The Agency collects notifications required by Article 3(4)(b) and Article 4(2) of REMIT mainly through electronic format, especially when data standards exist for information published under Regulations (EC) No 714/2009 and (EC) 715/2009. The relevant electronic format is published on the Agency's website.

text:
DOCUMENT: Comparison of 1st and 2nd edition of ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Market Abuse Prohibitions and Insider Dealing Detection
ID: 73
CONTENT:
Article 15 of REMIT requires that any person professionally arranging transactions in wholesale energy products who reasonably suspects a transaction might breach Articles 3 or 5 shall notify the NRA without further delay. Persons professionally arranging transactions must establish and maintain effective arrangements and procedures to identify breaches of Articles 3 or 5. The duty applies to any person professionally arranging transactions in wholesale energy products, including at least trading venues like energy exchanges and brokers. The Agency considers independent market surveillance departments in energy exchanges and compliance officers in brokers as best practices for effective arrangements to identify breaches of market abuse prohibitions and signals of suspicious transactions.

text:
DOCUMENT: Comparison of 1st and 2nd edition of ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Notification Regime and Market Abuse Prohibitions Overview
ID: 74
CONTENT:
The notification regime laid down by REMIT requires that persons subject to it decide on a case-by-case basis where there are reasonable grounds for suspicion concerning the relevant transaction. The market abuse prohibitions of REMIT are based on the Market Abuse Directive, but tailored to the gas and electricity markets. Market abuse means insider dealing and market manipulation, which have become explicitly prohibited with the entry into force of REMIT.

text:
DOCUMENT: Comparison of 1st and 2nd edition of ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Seven Types of Market Abuse Behavior
ID: 75
CONTENT:
The following seven types of behaviour may amount to market abuse: (1) Insider trading – when an insider trades, or tries to trade, in wholesale energy products on the basis of inside information relating to that wholesale energy product, Article 3(1)(a) of REMIT. (2) Improper disclosure of inside information – where an insider improperly discloses inside information to another person, unless such disclosure is made in the normal course of the exercise of their employment, profession or duties, Article 3(1)(b) of REMIT. (3) Recommending on the basis of inside information – where an insider is recommending or inducing, on the basis of inside information, another person to acquire or dispose of wholesale energy products to which that information relates, Article 3(1)(c) of REMIT.

ID: 76
CONTENT:

text:
DOCUMENT: Comparison of 1st and 2nd edition of ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Application of Insider Trading Prohibition and Definition of Insiders
ID: 78
CONTENT:
Whilst the prohibition of market manipulation applies to any engagement in, or attempt to engage in, market manipulation on wholesale energy markets by any person, the application of the prohibition of insider trading is limited to persons who possess inside information in relation to a wholesale energy product ('insider'). These include: (1) members of the administrative, management or supervisory bodies of an undertaking; (2) persons with holdings in the capital of an undertaking; (3) persons with access to the information through the exercise of their employment, profession or duties; (4) persons who have acquired such information through criminal activity; (5) persons who know, or ought to know, that it is inside information. Article 3(5) of REMIT clarifies that where the person who possesses inside information is a legal person, the prohibitions shall also apply to the natural persons who take part in the decision to carry out the transaction for the account of the legal person concerned.

text:
DOCUMENT: Comparison of 1st and 2nd edition of ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Attempted Insider Dealing and Prohibition Scope
ID: 79
CONTENT:
The prohibition of insider dealing contains elements of attempted behaviour. Article 3(1)(a) of REMIT not only prohibits from using inside information by acquiring or disposing of wholesale energy products to which that information relates but also prohibits from using inside information by trying to acquire or dispose of wholesale energy products to which that information relates.

text:
DOCUMENT: Comparison of 1st and 2nd edition of ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Exemptions from Insider Trading Prohibition - Transmission System Operators
ID: 80
CONTENT:
Paragraphs 3 and 4 of Article 3 of REMIT stipulate exemptions from the prohibition of insider trading. However, the exemptions may only apply for the prohibition of insider trading and are therefore neither exhaustive without prejudice of the obligation to publish inside information according to Article 4(1) of REMIT. Article 3(3) of REMIT stipulates that points (a) and (c) of paragraph 1 shall not apply to transmission system operators when purchasing electricity or natural gas in order to ensure the safe and secure operation of the system in accordance with their obligations under points (d) and (e) of Article 12 of Directive 2009/72/EC or points (a) and (c) of Article 13(1) of Directive 2009/73/EC.

text:
DOCUMENT: Comparison of 1st and 2nd edition of ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Exemptions from Insider Trading - Pre-existing Obligations
ID: 81
CONTENT:
Article 3(4)(a) of REMIT exempts transactions conducted in the discharge of an obligation that has become due to acquire or dispose of wholesale energy products where that obligation results from an agreement concluded, or an order to trade placed, before the person concerned came into possession of inside information. The Agency considers that this exemption also applies under the Market Abuse Directive and particularly applies to transactions in derivatives contracts conducted in the discharge of such obligations. Since the exemption also applies to orders to trade placed before the person concerned came into possession of inside information, the market participant is obliged to refrain from any amendment or selective withdrawal of the order placed ('hands-off approach') in order to comply with the prohibition of insider trading.

text:
DOCUMENT: Comparison of 1st and 2nd edition of ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Exemptions from Insider Trading - Unplanned Outages and Physical Loss
ID: 82
CONTENT:
Article 3(4)(b) of REMIT exempts transactions entered into by electricity and natural gas producers, operators of natural gas storage facilities or operators of LNG import facilities the sole purpose of which is to cover the immediate physical loss resulting from unplanned outages, where not to do so would result in the market participant not being able to meet existing contractual obligations or where such action is undertaken in agreement with the transmission system operator(s) concerned in order to ensure safe and secure operation of the system. In such a situation, the relevant information relating to the transactions shall be reported to the Agency and the national regulatory authority. The Agency considers that the exemption may only be applied for unplanned events, i.e. an event which is not ex-ante known by the primary owner of the data, that any physical loss needs to be caused immediately and solely through the unplanned event and that any transaction going beyond the immediate physical loss may not benefit from the exemption.

text:
DOCUMENT: Comparison of 1st and 2nd edition of ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Exemptions from Insider Trading - National Emergency Rules
ID: 83
CONTENT:
Article 3(4)(c) of REMIT exempts market participants acting under national emergency rules, where national authorities have intervened in order to secure the supply of electricity or natural gas and market mechanisms have been suspended in a Member State or parts thereof. In this case the authority competent for emergency planning shall ensure publication in accordance with Article 4. The Agency considers that this exemption will normally coincide with the exemption of Article 4(2) of REMIT and that in such case the authority competent for emergency planning shall ensure publication in accordance with Article 4(1) of REMIT.

text:
DOCUMENT: Comparison of 1st and 2nd edition of ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: TSO Restrictions on Information Disclosure
ID: 84
CONTENT:
The Agency understands that the exemption of Article 3(3) of REMIT does not apply to point (b) of paragraph 1 of this Article. Therefore, TSOs when purchasing electricity or natural gas in order to ensure the safe and secure operation of the system in accordance with their obligations under Directives 2009/72/EC and 2009/73/EC shall be prohibited from disclosing that information to any other person unless such disclosure is made in the normal course of the exercise of their employment, profession or duties.

text:
DOCUMENT: Comparison of 1st and 2nd edition of ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Contractual Obligations and Market Participant Assessment
ID: 85
CONTENT:
Regarding the exemption of Article 3(4)(b), the Agency considers that the contractual obligations referred to must exist ex-ante of the immediate physical loss resulting from unplanned outages. The existing contractual obligations must relate to the relevant period of the unplanned event. The Agency considers a market participant 'not being able' to meet such existing contractual obligations in particular transaction may be suspicious even if it matches none of the indications nor determinative factors. The market participant has no other own assets available to cover the loss. As regards the second alternative, the Agency considers that the criterion 'to ensure the safe and secure operation of the system' will mainly apply in cases of Article 3(4)(c) of REMIT.

text:
DOCUMENT: Comparison of 1st and 2nd edition of ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Delayed Disclosure of Inside Information Notification
ID: 86
CONTENT:
In case a market participant not only aims at applying the exemptions from the prohibition of insider trading according to Article 3(3) and (4) of REMIT, but also the exemption of Article 4(2) of REMIT concerning the delayed disclosure of inside information, the Agency and the relevant NRA(s) must be notified accordingly. According to Article 4(2) of REMIT, the market participant concerned shall without delay provide that information, together with a justification for the delay of the public disclosure, to the Agency and the relevant NRA having regard to Article 8(5) of REMIT, if the conditions of Article 4(2) of REMIT are met. Notification forms for delayed disclosure of inside information are available at the Agency's website.

text:
DOCUMENT: Comparison of 1st and 2nd edition of ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Application of Market Manipulation Prohibition and Attempted Manipulation
ID: 87
CONTENT:
REMIT does not only prohibit market manipulation, but also applies the concept of attempted market manipulation. Proving market manipulation would require a regulator to demonstrate that either a manipulative order was placed or a manipulative transaction was executed. However, there are situations where a person takes steps towards a manipulative behaviour and there is clear evidence of an intention to manipulate the market but either an order is not placed, or a transaction is not executed. The Regulation expressly prohibits attempts at market manipulation. This prohibition will enhance market integrity.

text:
DOCUMENT: Comparison of 1st and 2nd edition of ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Signals of Insider Dealing and Market Manipulation
ID: 89
CONTENT:
Signals are neither conclusive nor comprehensive and should only be regarded as a starting point when considering whether a transaction gives rise to indications of possible suspicious behaviour. They are to be applied using judgement rather than necessarily being interpreted literally. Transactions meeting the signals listed may be legitimate and hence not give reasonable grounds for suspicion.

Possible signals of insider dealing include: a) significant trading by major market participants before the announcement of information having a significant price effect; b) transactions resulting in sudden and unusual changes in the volume of orders and prices before the announcement of information having a significant price effect.

text:
DOCUMENT: Comparison of 1st and 2nd edition of ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Method of Reporting Suspicious Transactions
ID: 94
CONTENT:
Any person professionally arranging transactions in wholesale energy products who reasonably suspects that a transaction might breach Article 3 or 5 of REMIT shall notify the competent NRA without further delay of all relevant information available. Where not all the relevant information is available at the time of notification, the notification shall include at least the reasons why the notifying persons suspect that the transaction might constitute insider dealing or market manipulation. All remaining information shall be provided to the competent authority as soon as it becomes available. Notification can be effected by mail, electronic mail, telecopy or telephone, provided that in the latter case, written confirmation is provided upon request by the competent authority.

text:
DOCUMENT: Comparison of 1st and 2nd edition of ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Standard Reporting Format and Agency Recommendations
ID: 95
CONTENT:
The Agency considers that it would assist those subject to the obligation to report suspicious transactions if there were a standard reporting format for doing so. The Agency, based on the experiences in financial markets, therefore recommends using the format published on the Agency's website and urges NRAs to adopt it for suspicious transaction reporting to NRAs, the notification of which has to be forwarded to the Agency without delay pursuant to Article 16(2) of REMIT.

text:
DOCUMENT: Comparison of 1st and 2nd edition of ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Obligations of Persons Professionally Arranging Transactions
ID: 96
CONTENT:
Persons making suspicious transactions reports do not need to have all the required information before contacting the competent authority. If the case is one for which there is a need to alert the competent authority urgently, then the Agency would expect that NRAs receive notifications as soon as possible, even before all aspects of the transaction and all related information become known. This contact may take place by telephone if appropriate, giving the basic details and reasons for suspicion. The other information can be supplied subsequently.

text:
DOCUMENT: Comparison of 1st and 2nd edition of ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Duty to Establish and Maintain Effective Arrangements and Procedures
ID: 97
CONTENT:
Article 15 of REMIT requires that persons professionally arranging transactions in wholesale energy products who reasonably suspect that a transaction might breach Articles 3 or 5 shall notify the NRA without further delay. Persons professionally arranging transactions in wholesale energy products shall establish and maintain effective arrangements and procedures to identify breaches of Articles 3 or 5. The regulation and its implementing measures do not deal with the steps which the persons subject to this requirement need to take to identify such transactions. Those who are subject to the requirement clearly need to ensure that they comply with this obligation.

text:
DOCUMENT: Comparison of 1st and 2nd edition of ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Persons Subject to REMIT Article 15 Requirements
ID: 98
CONTENT:
The duty to establish and maintain effective arrangements and procedures to identify breaches of Articles 3 or 5 of REMIT is on any person professionally arranging transactions in wholesale energy products. These include at least trading venues like energy exchanges and brokers. Concerning gas hubs, the Agency considers that normally the TSO operates the gas hub, but it might be the case that gas hubs operate separately from the TSO. At gas hubs transfer of title (ownership) takes places, which can be considered a transaction. Thus the person owning the gas hub can be considered as a person professionally arranging transactions according to REMIT Article 15.

text:
DOCUMENT: Comparison of 1st and 2nd edition of ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Data Availability and Surveillance at Gas Hubs and TSOs
ID: 99
CONTENT:
It should be noted that the depth of data available to hubs varies on a hub-by-hub basis. Certain hubs will be unable to conduct surveillance (for example, a hub receiving highly aggregated data without price details), with market monitoring being conducted elsewhere (e.g. at an Exchange). TSOs or persons acting on their behalf may have to be regarded as being persons professionally arranging transactions insofar as they are arranging balancing markets. The Agency currently considers independent market surveillance departments in the case of energy exchanges and compliance officers in the case of brokers as best practices of effective arrangements to identify breaches of the prohibitions of market abuse.

DOCUMENT: Comparison of 1st and 2nd edition of ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Best Practices for Market Surveillance and Compliance
ID: 100
CONTENT:
Applicable rules for market surveillance and compliance in the EU financial market legislation may serve as a guidance to establish and maintain such mechanisms. The notification regime laid down by REMIT requires that persons subject to it decide on a case-by-case basis where there are reasonable grounds for suspicion concerning the relevant transaction. The indications given are therefore neither exhaustive nor determinative.

text:
DOCUMENT: Comparison of 1st and 2nd edition of ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Application of Prohibitions of Market Abuse - Introduction
ID: 101
CONTENT:
According to Article 13(1), first subparagraph, of REMIT, NRAs shall ensure that the prohibitions set out in Articles 3 and 5 and the obligation set out in Article 4 thereof are applied. In the interim phase until data collection according to Article 8 of the Regulation applies and the investigatory and enforcement powers are implemented at national level according to Articles 13(2) of the Regulation and penalties according to Article 18 of the Regulation apply, NRAs should make use of their existing powers, in particular those powers conferred to them with the national implementation of the Third Energy Package, to ensure that market integrity and transparency of wholesale energy markets are aimed at with the entry into force of REMIT.

text:
DOCUMENT: Comparison of 1st and 2nd edition of ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Accepted Market Practices (AMPs) Regime
ID: 102
CONTENT:
According to Recital 27 of REMIT, the Agency's guidance should address inter alia the issue of accepted market practices. Article 2(2)(a)(ii) and (3)(a)(ii) of REMIT stipulate that accepted market practices such as those applying in the financial services area, which are currently defined by Article 1(5) of Directive 2003/6/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 28 January 2003 on insider dealing and market manipulation (market abuse) and which may be adapted if that Directive is amended, could be a legitimate way for market participants to secure a favourable price for a wholesale energy product.

text:
DOCUMENT: Comparison of 1st and 2nd edition of ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Definition of Accepted Market Practices
ID: 103
CONTENT:
According to Article 1(5) of Directive 2003/6/EC, "Accepted market practices" means practices that are reasonably expected in one or more financial markets and are accepted by the competent authority in accordance with guidelines adopted by the Commission in accordance with the procedure laid down in Article 17(2) of Directive 2003/6/EC. Under Directive 2003/6/EC, the concept of accepted market practices may either apply in relation to market manipulation according to Article 1(2) of Directive 2003/6/EC, or in relation to the information which users of commodity derivatives markets would expect to be made public concerning market activities.

text:
DOCUMENT: Comparison of 1st and 2nd edition of ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Accepted Market Practices (AMPs) under REMIT - Overview and Distinctions
ID: 104
CONTENT:
Commodity derivatives according to Article 1(1) of Directive 2003/6/EC. The Agency concludes the following as regards Accepted Market Practices (AMPs) under REMIT: Firstly, the AMPs accepted by competent authorities according to Directive 2003/6/EC may also apply under REMIT, but AMPs under REMIT are not limited to these accepted market practices. Accordingly, new AMPs may be established under REMIT, in particular concerning wholesale energy commodity markets. Secondly, the same way financial market authorities have consistently made a distinction between practices and activities; also the Agency will distinguish between practices and activities carried out in wholesale energy markets. 'Activities' would cover different types of operations or strategies that may be undertaken such as arbitrage, hedging and short selling. 'Market practices' would cover the way these activities are handled and executed in the market.

text:
DOCUMENT: Comparison of 1st and 2nd edition of ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Activities vs. Market Practices - AMP Status Considerations
ID: 105
CONTENT:
'Activities' are considered too broad to qualify for the status of AMPs. An 'activity' such as hedging could be undertaken in different ways. If the activity is carried out in a way which does not constitute market manipulation, then the question of giving it accepted market practice status does not arise. On the other hand, if the 'activity' is carried out in a way which would constitute market manipulation, it is unlikely that a competent authority would be prepared to accept it as an AMP. Hence to give an 'activity' a blanket AMP status would neither be meaningful nor desirable. Thirdly, the Agency agrees with financial market authorities on their considerations of the issue of whether certain more specific practices, such as crossing/pre-arranged trades or gross bidding, should be given accepted market practice status, subject to the condition that these practices should be undertaken according to the rules of the relevant organised market place applicable to their conduct.

text:
DOCUMENT: Comparison of 1st and 2nd edition of ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: National Responsibility and Coordination of AMPs
ID: 106
CONTENT:
As in most of such cases, conduct of the practice in conformity with the rules of the organised market place would be sufficient in itself to promote market integrity and therefore the question of giving the practice accepted market practice status would not arise. Lastly, the decision whether a process constitutes an AMP or not is a matter of national or regional specificities. AMPs, therefore, are primarily the responsibility of individual NRAs and so a practice which one competent authority considers is an AMP, may not be viewed as such by another. However, each NRA has a duty to consult, both nationally and with other relevant NRAs, and to coordinate with the Agency prior to disclosing any market practices that they have accepted. There is also an obligation on the Agency to coordinate and publish the AMPs on its website. These will be published in a standard ACER format and a link provided to the national legal text once they have been recognised and have undergone the requisite national and European consultation process.

text:
DOCUMENT: Comparison of 1st and 2nd edition of ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Factors for Assessing Market Practices - Transparency and Market Forces
ID: 107
CONTENT:
The following non-exhaustive list of factors shall be taken into account by competent authorities when assessing particular practices in wholesale energy markets: The level of transparency of the relevant market practice to the whole market: Transparency of market practices by market participants is crucial for considering whether a particular market practice can be accepted by competent authorities. The less transparent a practice is, the more likely it is not to be accepted. However, practices on non-regulated markets might for structural reasons be less transparent than similar practices on regulated markets. Such practices should not be in themselves considered as unacceptable by competent authorities. The need to safeguard the operation of market forces and the proper interplay of the forces of supply and demand: Market practices inhibiting the interaction of supply and demand by limiting the opportunities for other market participants to respond to transactions can create higher risks for market integrity and are, therefore, less likely to be accepted by competent authorities.

text:
DOCUMENT: Comparison of 1st and 2nd edition of ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Assessment Factors - Liquidity, Efficiency, and Market Impact
ID: 108
CONTENT:
The degree to which the relevant market practice has an impact on market liquidity and efficiency: Market practices which enhance liquidity and efficiency are more likely to be accepted than those reducing them. The degree to which the relevant practice takes into account the trading mechanism of the relevant market and enables market participants to react properly and in a timely manner to the new market situation created by that practice. The risk inherent in the relevant practice for the integrity of, directly or indirectly, related markets, whether regulated or not, in the relevant wholesale energy product within the whole Union. The outcome of any investigation of the relevant market practice by any competent authority, in particular whether the relevant market practice breached rules or regulations designed to prevent market abuse, or codes of conduct, be it on the market in question or on directly or indirectly related markets within the Union.

text:
DOCUMENT: Comparison of 1st and 2nd edition of ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Structural Characteristics and Overriding Principles for AMPs
ID: 109
CONTENT:
The structural characteristics of the relevant market including whether it is regulated or not, the types of wholesale energy products traded and the type of market participants. Overriding principles to be observed by competent authorities to ensure that accepted market practices do not undermine market integrity, while fostering innovation and the continued dynamic development of wholesale energy markets: new or emerging accepted market practices should not be assumed to be unacceptable by the competent authority simply because they have not been previously accepted by it. Practising fairness and efficiency by market participants is required in order not to create prejudice to normal market activity and market integrity. Competent authorities should analyse the impact of the relevant market practice before carrying out the relevant market practice.

text:
DOCUMENT: Comparison of 1st and 2nd edition of ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Application of AMPs Regime - Inside Information Disclosure
ID: 110
CONTENT:
The Agency currently considers the application of the AMPs regime only in relation to the information which users of wholesale energy markets would expect to be made public concerning wholesale energy products for the following incidents and possibly in coordination with the competent national financial market authority: Disclosure of inside information through regional or national inside information platforms fulfilling the RIS requirements mentioned above if nominated by the competent NRA(s) following a public consultation and notified to the Agency. NRAs should aim at regional platforms agreed on with relevant NRAs for relevant markets. Disclosure of inside information in an aggregated/anonymised way in order to comply with competition law and notified to the Agency if considered necessary at national level and agreed upon by the national NRA with the national competition authority and notified to the Agency. Definition of national/regional thresholds for the disclosure of inside information in relevant wholesale gas markets following consultation of market participants and accepted by the competent NRA(s) and notified to the Agency.

text:
DOCUMENT: Comparison of 1st and 2nd edition of ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Compliance Regime for REMIT Requirements
ID: 111
CONTENT:
The Agency is of the opinion that market participants should develop a clear compliance regime towards real time or close to real time disclosure of inside information and the further REMIT requirements, beyond compliance with existing Third Package transparency obligations. NRAs should consider the following best practice example of such compliance regime for market participants, but taking into account the market participant's size and trading capacity: Compliance culture: the creation of a corporate culture to comply with REMIT requirements. Compliance objectives: the compliance with REMIT requirements, namely the registration, disclosure and reporting obligations and the market abuse prohibitions. Compliance organisation: the definition of roles and responsibilities in the internal organisation (e.g. responsibilities for the REMIT requirements (centralised vs. decentralised), internal vs. external reporting lines, internal vs. external interfaces, provision of resources: human / technical (IT Systems) resources).

ID: 112
CONTENT:
Compliance risks: the identification / assessment of concrete compliance risks. Compliance programme: the identification of concrete actions to define compliant/non-compliant behaviour. DOCUMENT: Comparison of 1st and 2nd edition of ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Penalty Regimes for REMIT Infringements
ID: 113
CONTENT:
When Member States lay down the rules on penalties applicable to infringements of REMIT and take all measures necessary to ensure that they are implemented according to Article 18 of the Regulation, NRAs should work towards penalties for all potential infringements of REMIT which may consist of breaches of the market abuse prohibitions of Articles 3 and 5 of the Regulation, but also of breaches of the obligation to notify the relevant information to the Agency and the competent NRA in situations according to Article 3(4)(b) of the Regulation, the obligation to disclose inside information according to Article 4(1) of the Regulation, the obligation to notify the Agency and the competent NRA of delayed disclosure of inside information according to Article 4(2) of the Regulation, the obligation to provide the Agency with a record of wholesale energy market transactions, including orders to trade, according to Article 8(1) of the Regulation, the obligation to register with the competent NRA according to Article 8(1) of the Regulation, and the obligations of persons professionally arranging transactions according to Article 15 of the Regulation.

source: Consultation Paper ACER REMIT Fees amendment.pdf
text:
DOCUMENT: Consultation Paper ACER REMIT Fees amendment.pdf
SECTION: Introduction and Background
ID: 0
CONTENT:
This public consultation is part of the preparations for a Commission Decision amending Commission Decision (EU) 2020/2152 of 17 December 2020 on fees due to the European Union Agency for the Cooperation of Energy Regulators for tasks under Regulation (EU) No 1227/2011 of 25 October 2011 on wholesale energy market integrity and transparency ('REMIT'). The objective is to update the Fee Decision setting fees due to ACER for collecting, handling, processing and analysing of information reported under REMIT. This update is necessary since Regulation (EU) 2024/1106 of 11 April 2024 amends REMIT and the provisions on fees in Article 32 of Regulation (EU) 2019/942 establishing ACER. This public consultation is required under Article 32(2) of the ACER Regulation. The ideas presented have been developed by DG Energy and ACER for this consultation and are without prejudice to the Commission college's decision on the planned Commission Decision.

source: Consultation Paper ACER REMIT Fees amendment.pdf
text:
DOCUMENT: Consultation Paper ACER REMIT Fees amendment.pdf
SECTION: Legislative Background and ACER Regulation
ID: 1
CONTENT:
Regulation (EU) 2019/942 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 5 June 2019 establishing the European Union Agency for the Cooperation of Energy Regulators ('ACER Regulation') introduced fees as an additional funding source to cover costs of REMIT related activities performed by ACER. Pursuant to Article 32(2), fees and payment methods are set by the Commission. The Fee Decision complements Article 32 of the ACER Regulation. Regulation (EU) 2024/1106 of 11 April 2024 amends Article 32 of the ACER Regulation, establishing that fees are due to ACER for: (a) requesting exemption decisions and decisions on cross-border cost allocation; (b) collecting, handling, processing and analysing information reported by market participants pursuant to Article 8 of Regulation (EU) No 1227/2011 and for disclosing inside information. Fees are paid by registered reporting mechanisms and inside information platforms. Revenues may also cover costs of ACER's supervision and investigatory powers under Articles 13 to 13c and Article 16 of REMIT.

source: Consultation Paper ACER REMIT Fees amendment.pdf
text:
DOCUMENT: Consultation Paper ACER REMIT Fees amendment.pdf
SECTION: Fee Setting Requirements and Principles
ID: 2
CONTENT:
According to Article 32(2) of the amended ACER Regulation, fees and payment methods shall be set by the Commission after carrying out a public consultation and after consulting the Administrative Board and the Board of Regulators. The fees shall be proportionate to the costs of relevant services provided in a cost-effective way and shall be sufficient to cover those costs. Fees must be set at a level ensuring they are non-discriminatory and avoid placing undue financial or administrative burden on market participants or entities acting on their behalf. The Commission shall regularly examine the level of fees based on evaluation and, if necessary, adapt the level and payment methods. The Fee Decision needs updating to reflect changes to Article 32, specifically: extending fee-paying requirements to Inside Information Platforms (IIPs) and extending the scope of eligible costs to new supervision and investigatory powers given to ACER by the REMIT amendment.

source: Consultation Paper ACER REMIT Fees amendment.pdf
text:
DOCUMENT: Consultation Paper ACER REMIT Fees amendment.pdf
SECTION: Current Fee Scheme Structure
ID: 3
CONTENT:
The basic structure of the fee scheme pursuant to the current Fee Decision operates as follows: (1) Total costs to be covered by fees are identified in the programming document adopted by ACER's Administrative Board at year-end. (2) At year beginning, ACER calculates fees payable by each Registered Reporting Mechanism (RRM) based on previous year data. Fees consist of three components: a flat enrolment fee component; a transaction records-based fee component depending on the number of market participants reporting via the RRM and records generated at different organised or non-organised market places; and an amount to balance differences between the transaction records-based fee component paid in the previous year and what would have been paid according to actual reporting. (3) If total fees exceed eligible costs, individual amounts payable by each RRM are reduced pro-rata. (4) ACER sends invoices (debit notes) to reporting parties. (5) The cycle repeats annually.

source: Consultation Paper ACER REMIT Fees amendment.pdf
text:
DOCUMENT: Consultation Paper ACER REMIT Fees amendment.pdf
SECTION: Experience with Fee Decision Implementation
ID: 4
CONTENT:
The Commission considers that ACER and stakeholders successfully implemented the Fee Decision and that overall it has fulfilled its objective of providing ACER with additional funding without placing undue financial or administrative burden on stakeholders. Nevertheless, the planned amendment provides an opportunity to adjust the Fee Decision based on experience with implementation since 2021, including clarification concerning calculation of the correction amount, which should be calculated by subtracting the transaction records-based fee component paid after the reduction factor is applied in the previous year. Stakeholders are consulted on their experience with the Fee Decision and its implementation, whether they see need to correct certain aspects, and what changes should be made.

source: Consultation Paper ACER REMIT Fees amendment.pdf
text:
DOCUMENT: Consultation Paper ACER REMIT Fees amendment.pdf
SECTION: Inside Information Platforms (IIPs) Fee Proposals
ID: 5
CONTENT:
Pursuant to Article 4a of the amended REMIT and once the Commission Regulation (delegated act) supplementing this Article is adopted by 8 May 2025, ACER will be in charge of authorising and supervising Inside Information Platforms (IIPs), going beyond the current registration of such entities by ACER. The Commission proposes that each IIP would need to pay annually a flat enrolment fee equivalent to the one paid by Registered Reporting Mechanisms (RRMs). A similar transaction records-based fee component for transaction reporting should not be required for the publication of inside information. Stakeholders are consulted on whether they agree with these proposals regarding fees to be paid by IIPs.

source: Consultation Paper ACER REMIT Fees amendment.pdf
text:
DOCUMENT: Consultation Paper ACER REMIT Fees amendment.pdf
SECTION: Rising Costs and Inflation Impact
ID: 6
CONTENT:
ACER's costs for implementing REMIT have risen considerably: from around EUR 8.8 million costs eligible for funding by fees in 2021 to around EUR 12.4 million in 2024. Costs are expected to further increase given ACER's additional tasks according to the REMIT revision, with costs eligible for funding by fees estimated at around EUR 17.3 million in 2025. Inflation, more high-frequency trading, and additional tasks under REMIT are the three main reasons for rising costs which have not been matched by increasing fee revenues. Inflation developments since 2021 demonstrate this is a factor to consider for the revision of the Commission decision on REMIT fees. Budget numbers for 2025 and 2026 are taken from ACER's Programming Document 2024-2026 and do not include all costs based on REMIT revision.

source: Consultation Paper ACER REMIT Fees amendment.pdf
text:
DOCUMENT: Consultation Paper ACER REMIT Fees amendment.pdf
SECTION: Market Changes and High-Frequency Trading
ID: 7
CONTENT:
Changes in the market, especially more high-frequency trading, have resulted in an exponential increase of collected records not correlating with an equivalent increase of fee revenue. Since 2021, the number of reported transaction records under REMIT has increased by around 50% each year. It is currently expected that the number will further increase once additional data types are added under a revised REMIT implementing regulation. Currently, the highest fee subcomponent per data cluster is EUR 16,000 for more than 100 million transaction records in case of wholesale energy products in relation to supply of electricity and gas using an organised market place or in case of wholesale energy products in relation to transportation of electricity and gas, and EUR 16,000 for more than 10 million transaction records in case of wholesale energy products in relation to supply of electricity and gas traded outside an organised market place. The increase in reported transaction records is not resulting in equivalent increase in fee revenues, since due to high-frequency trading more market participants pay EUR 16,000 per data cluster despite reporting many more than 100 million transaction records.

source: Consultation Paper ACER REMIT Fees amendment.pdf
text:
DOCUMENT: Consultation Paper ACER REMIT Fees amendment.pdf
SECTION: REMIT 2024 Amendments and Expanded ACER Tasks
ID: 8
CONTENT:
The amendments to REMIT in 2024 increase the scope and depth of ACER's tasks, notably: ACER will be in charge of authorising and supervising Inside Information Platforms (IIPs) and Registered Reporting Mechanisms (RRMs), going beyond current registration; ACER now has the task of collecting all suspicious transaction or order reports which all persons professionally arranging or executing transactions across the EU must report; ACER now has complementary powers to investigate potential breaches of REMIT if two or more Member States are concerned. The legislative financial statement accompanying the Commission's proposal for amending REMIT estimates that in total 25 additional full-time equivalents (FTE) will be needed, phased in from 2024 onwards to 2027. ACER will receive additional funding from the EU budget, but costs for enhancing the REMIT IT system and for at least two thirds of additional staff will need to be funded by fees.

text:
DOCUMENT: Consultation Paper ACER REMIT Fees amendment.pdf
SECTION: Hydrogen Market Extension and Additional Staffing
ID: 9
CONTENT:
Article 83 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1789 on the internal market for renewable gas, natural gas and hydrogen extends REMIT to wholesale hydrogen markets. The legislative financial statement accompanying the Commission proposal for revising the Gas Regulation estimates that this will require in total 7 additional FTE, phased in from 2024 onwards to 2027. All those staff will need to be funded by fees. These additional staffing requirements, combined with the 25 FTE needed for REMIT amendments, represent significant cost increases that must be covered through the fee mechanism.

source: Consultation Paper ACER REMIT Fees amendment.pdf
text:
DOCUMENT: Consultation Paper ACER REMIT Fees amendment.pdf
SECTION: Transaction Records-Based Fee Component - Overview and Data Clusters
ID: 12
CONTENT:
The Commission proposes to add additional data clusters beyond the current highest data clusters of more than 10 million transaction records (for supply contracts not using an organised marketplace) or more than 100 million transaction records (for all other contracts) and to increase the level of the fee subcomponent for each data cluster. One option is to add additional data clusters for each additional 10 million / 100 million transaction records. Another option is to add data clusters continuing the current progression of number of transaction records, meaning the next data cluster would be more than 10 million to up to 100 million transaction records / to more than 100 million to up to 1 billion transaction records. Data clusters could also be defined according to a formula in-between those two options.

source: Consultation Paper ACER REMIT Fees amendment.pdf
text:
DOCUMENT: Consultation Paper ACER REMIT Fees amendment.pdf
SECTION: Fee Subcomponents Structure and Current Pricing
ID: 13
CONTENT:
The fee subcomponents per data cluster for transaction records are outlined in Articles 6.2 and 6.3 of the Fee Decision. Currently, the fee subcomponents per data cluster for transaction records range from EUR 250 for 1 to 1,000 records, increasing by a factor of 2x for each subsequent cluster, up to EUR 16,000 for records exceeding 100 million transaction records. For data clusters exceeding 100 million transaction records, the fee subcomponent is currently fixed at 16,000 EUR. A similar logic applies to the fee subcomponents outlined in Article 6.3 of the Fee Decision, where the pricing structure follows the same incremental approach.

source: Consultation Paper ACER REMIT Fees amendment.pdf
text:
DOCUMENT: Consultation Paper ACER REMIT Fees amendment.pdf
SECTION: Proposed Amendments to Fee Subcomponents
ID: 14
CONTENT:
The Commission proposes three amendments: First, for each of Articles 6.2 and 6.3 of the Fee Decision, increase the level of the fee subcomponent for the first data cluster by 20%, meaning EUR 300 (instead of EUR 250) ('First Amendment'). Second, regarding fee subcomponents for further data clusters, one option is to keep the current factor of two according to which the levels increase for each additional data cluster ('Second Amendment, Option 1'). An alternative option would be to increase the fee subcomponents by a higher factor, e.g. 2.1 or 2.2 ('Second Amendment, Option 2'). Third, add more data clusters to reflect the increasing use of high-frequency trading, with new lines in Article 6.2 applying to every additional 100 million transaction records, and in Article 6.3 applying to every additional 10 million transaction records ('Third Amendment').

text:
DOCUMENT: Consultation Paper ACER REMIT Fees amendment.pdf
SECTION: Additional Annual Supervisory Fee for RRMs and IIPs
ID: 16
CONTENT:
To ensure fees cover eligible costs incurred by ACER and reflect its increased mandate, an option is to add an annual supervisory fee for Registered Reporting Mechanisms (RRMs) and Investment Firms Providing Investment Services (IIPs). For RRMs, the basis would be the planned budget for transaction information related costs, from which estimated revenue from flat enrolment and transaction record-based fees would be deducted. Remaining costs would be split among all RRMs according to their share of total transaction records. A minimum annual supervisory fee of EUR 15,000 to EUR 25,000 per RRM could be set. For IIPs, the basis would be the planned budget for inside information related costs, from which flat enrolment fee revenue would be deducted. Remaining costs could be split equally or according to share of Urgent Market Message records. A minimum annual supervisory fee of EUR 5,000 to EUR 10,000 per IIP could be set.

text:
DOCUMENT: Consultation Paper ACER REMIT Fees amendment.pdf
SECTION: Automatic Adjustment to Inflation
ID: 17
CONTENT:
Fee schemes for other agencies such as the EU Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) and EU Agency for Railways (ERA) provide for automatic indexation of fees to inflation, using tools such as Eurostat's Harmonised Indices of Consumer Prices (HICP) or annual updates of remuneration of EU officials. Such indexation could provide stability to the fee scheme by avoiding the need for regular revisions of the Fee Decision. It could also allow for more careful increase of fee levels in amendments, since without indexation the increase would need to account for possible inflation-driven higher costs in the future.

text:
DOCUMENT: Consultation Paper ACER REMIT Fees amendment.pdf
SECTION: Consultation Questions and Final Remarks
ID: 18
CONTENT:
The Commission seeks consultation on: appropriate levels for flat enrolment fees; whether to increase the current factor of two for fee subcomponent increases and to what level (e.g., 2.1, 2.2, or other); views on all amendments and options considered; opinions on additional annual supervisory fee components and alternative options to ensure fee revenues cover eligible costs; views on how the Fee Decision could provide for cost increases due to inflation; and any other comments or recommendations. The Commission proposes to maintain the basic structure of the fee scheme as laid down in the Fee Decision. Contact: DG Energy, Unit C3 – Internal Energy Market, Email: ENER-MARKET-DESIGN@ec.europa.eu

DOCUMENT: Edison Aggiornamento Registro REMIT.pdf
SECTION: 1.1 Objective of the Document
ID: 2
CONTENT:
Il presente documento, allegato alla Policy Commodity Market Abuse N.G. 09/2018, ha lo scopo di descrivere il processo di Aggiornamento del Registro REMIT. Obiettivo del processo è assicurare che vengano svolte e indirizzate, da parte della Funzione Compliance & Business Support, tutte le attività necessarie al fine di mantenere aggiornata la registrazione ai fini REMIT di Edison Spa e di tutte le società del Gruppo. L'attività di indirizzo si inquadra nelle responsabilità di supporto della Funzione Compliance & Business Support così come delineate nella Disposizione Organizzativa N°64/2023 e nella Comunicazione Interna 01/24 che, coerentemente con quanto definito dalla 'Linea Guida applicativa del modello di governance della compliance', identifica l'Owner di Materia e i Compliance Focal Point a livello di Gruppo a cui è assegnata la responsabilità di definire e presidiare il framework di compliance al Regolamento REMIT.

ID: 3
CONTENT:
La Norma Generale N°09/18, per quanto riguarda l'obbligo di registrazione di cui all'art. 9 del Regolamento, stabilisce che ogni Società o Divisione del Gruppo Edison che risulta essere soggetta al presente obbligo, è tenuta, per quanto di competenza e ove opportuno, a formalizzare mediante l'adozione di adeguate procedure le attività, i ruoli e le responsabilità per il processo di registrazione REMIT ed è tenuta, qualora fosse necessario, all'aggiornamento tempestivo dei dati comunicati ad ARERA in conformità a quanto richiesto dallo stesso Regolamento. La Funzione Compliance & Business Support al fine di garantire un tempestivo aggiornamento del Registro REMIT da parte delle diverse strutture del Gruppo Edison presiede l'attività in oggetto come di seguito descritto nell'Allegato VIII.

SECTION: Internal Procedure and Compliance Responsibilities
ID: 4
CONTENT:
La Procedura Interna N°04/18 della Divisione Gas & Power Portfolio Management & Optimization a sua volta prevede che la Funzione Compliance, in seguito alle segnalazioni ricevute dalla Direzione Corporate Affairs & Governance o qualora venga a conoscenza di cambiamenti societari intercorsi per mezzo di altri canali ufficiali (e.g. emissione di una nuova Disposizione Organizzativa), è responsabile di: a) Verificare se la segnalazione sia rilevante al fine dell'aggiornamento del Registro REMIT e aggiornare di conseguenza il DB REMIT; b) Segnalare agli Amministratori Delegati delle società controllate di Edison S.p.A. la necessità di valutare se le variazioni intercorse all'assetto societario possono richiedere l'iscrizione della società di propria competenza all'interno del Registro REMIT o, qualora già registrata, l'aggiornamento dei relativi dati; c) Valutare la necessità di aggiornare i dati relativi a Edison S.p.A. nel Registro REMIT, eventualmente con il supporto degli Amministratori Delegati delle società controllate o con il supporto di specifici referenti di compliance da quest'ultimi indicati, e, nel caso, procedere tempestivamente all'aggiornamento degli stessi dati.

DOCUMENT: Edison Compliance agli obblighi del regolamento REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Recipients and Definitions - Part 1
ID: 3
CONTENT:
Destinatari della presente procedura sono la Divisione Midstream e le Unità Organizzative del Gruppo Edison coinvolte nell'esecuzione delle attività necessarie ad adempiere alle prescrizioni del Regolamento REMIT. Definizioni principali: ACER - Agency for the Cooperation of Energy Regulators, Agenzia di coordinamento delle Autorità Europee di regolazione dei mercati energetici. ARERA - Autorità di Regolazione per Energia, Reti e Ambiente che svolge attività di regolazione e controllo nei settori dell'energia elettrica, del gas naturale, dei servizi idrici, del ciclo dei rifiuti e del telecalore. È l'Autorità competente in Italia per l'attuazione e l'applicazione del Regolamento REMIT nonché delle sanzioni derivanti dalla violazione degli obblighi e dei divieti previsti.

DOCUMENT: Edison Compliance agli obblighi del regolamento REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Definitions - Part 2: Contracts and Data
ID: 4
CONTENT:
Contratto OTC (Over The Counter): Contratto tra due operatori di mercato avente ad oggetto un prodotto energetico all'ingrosso sottoscritto senza l'utilizzo dei servizi di intermediazione offerti da broker, mercati ed exchange. DB REMIT: Registro informatico gestito e aggiornato dalla Funzione COMP al fine di tenere traccia delle Società del Gruppo Edison rilevanti ai fini del Regolamento REMIT. Fundamental Data: Informazioni riguardanti la capacità e l'uso degli impianti di produzione, stoccaggio, consumo o trasmissione di energia elettrica e di gas naturale o quelle riguardanti la capacità e l'uso di impianti GNL, inclusa l'indisponibilità pianificata o non pianificata di tali impianti.

metadata.original_text: Contratto OTC (Over The Counter): Contratto tra due operatori di mercato avente ad oggetto un prodotto energetico all'ingrosso sottoscritto senza l'utilizzo dei servizi di intermediazione offerti da broker, mercati ed exchange. DB REMIT: Registro informatico gestito e aggiornato dalla Funzione COMP al fine di tenere traccia delle Società del Gruppo Edison rilevanti ai fini del Regolamento REMIT. Fundamental Data: Informazioni riguardanti la capacità e l'uso degli impianti di produzione, stoccaggio, consumo o trasmissione di energia elettrica e di gas naturale o quelle riguardanti la capacità e l'uso di impianti GNL, inclusa l'indisponibilità pianificata o non pianificata di tali impianti.

text:
DOCUMENT: Edison Compliance agli obblighi del regolamento REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Definitions - Part 3: Privileged Information and Platforms
ID: 5
CONTENT:
Informazione privilegiata: Come definito dall'art. 2 del Regolamento REMIT, un'informazione che ha carattere preciso, che non è stata resa pubblica, che concerne, direttamente o indirettamente, uno o più prodotti energetici all'ingrosso e che, se resa pubblica, potrebbe verosimilmente influire in modo sensibile sui prezzi di tali prodotti. Inside Information Platform (IIP): Soggetto autorizzato da ACER a fornire il servizio di gestione di una piattaforma per la pubblicazione di informazioni privilegiate. Piattaforma Informazioni Privilegiate (PiP): Piattaforma di pubblicazione delle informazioni privilegiate, autorizzata da ACER e messa a disposizione dal GME al fine di consentire agli operatori di mercato di adempiere agli obblighi di trasparenza previsti dal Regolamento REMIT.

DOCUMENT: Edison Compliance agli obblighi del regolamento REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Definitions - Part 4: Market Operators and Systems
ID: 6
CONTENT:
LNG System Operator (LSO): Soggetto che gestisce un impianto utilizzato per le operazioni di liquefazione del gas naturale, l'importazione, lo scarico, la rigassificazione di GNL e il relativo stoccaggio. Operatore di mercato: Persona, inclusi i gestori dei sistemi di trasmissione (TSO), che esegue operazioni (contratti), compresa la trasmissione di ordini di compravendita, in uno o più mercati energetici all'ingrosso. Mercato Organizzato: Un sistema multilaterale, o qualsiasi altro sistema, che consente o facilita l'incontro di molteplici interessi di terzi relativi all'acquisto e alla vendita di prodotti energetici all'ingrosso in modo che si traducano in un contratto. Esempi: borse dell'energia elettrica e del gas e piattaforme di trading gestite da broker.

text:
DOCUMENT: Edison Compliance agli obblighi del regolamento REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Definitions - Part 5: Market and Registration
ID: 7
CONTENT:
Mercato del Giorno Prima (MGP): Sessione di negoziazione gestita dal GME dove si negozia e conclude la maggior parte delle transazioni di compravendita di energia elettrica con consegna sul mercato italiano. Sul MGP si scambiano blocchi orari di energia per il giorno successivo. Gli operatori partecipano presentando offerte nelle quali indicano la quantità ed il prezzo massimo/minimo al quale sono disposti ad acquistare/vendere. Registro REMIT: Registro dei partecipanti ai mercati delle commodity energetiche; l'iscrizione è obbligatoria per gli operatori che eseguono transazioni rilevanti ai fini del reporting REMIT. Il Registro per gli operatori italiani è tenuto e aggiornato da ARERA che a sua volta rende disponibili i dati trasmettendoli al Registro Europeo tenuto e aggiornato da ACER.

SECTION: Definitions - Part 6: Wholesale Energy Products and Reporting
ID: 8
CONTENT:
Prodotto energetico all'ingrosso: Contratti fisici e finanziari aventi ad oggetto, o come sottostante, energia elettrica o gas naturale e i relativi contratti di trasporto la cui consegna avvenga nell'Unione Europea. Registered Reporting Mechanism (RRM): Soggetto certificato da ACER a fornire servizi di reporting in ambito REMIT. Sono gli unici soggetti abilitati a trasmettere i dati del reporting REMIT ad ACER. Matrice RACI: Matrice che descrive in forma tabellare le responsabilità e i ruoli assegnati alle diverse strutture coinvolte nella specifica attività/processo.

text:
DOCUMENT: Edison Compliance agli obblighi del regolamento REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Utente del Dispacciamento
ID: 15
CONTENT:
Il soggetto che conclude con Terna S.p.A. un contratto per il servizio di dispacciamento si definisce Utente del Dispacciamento. L'Utente del Dispacciamento è l'unico soggetto abilitato a presentare programmi di immissione in rete per uno specifico punto (generalmente un impianto di produzione / generazione) oggetto del contratto di dispacciamento. Tale programma viene venduto sul mercato del giorno prima (MGP), può essere modificato sui mercati infragiornalieri (MI-XBID) e può essere ulteriormente modificato sul mercato dei servizi di dispacciamento (MSD – nel caso di impianti abilitati a partecipare a tale mercato).

text:
DOCUMENT: Edison Compliance agli obblighi del regolamento REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Variazioni della Disponibilità - Non Programmata e Programmata
ID: 16
CONTENT:
Variazione della disponibilità non programmata: Variazione non programmata della potenza che un'unità di produzione può erogare; può essere dovuta a cause sia di natura tecnica (anticipazione, prolungamento o accorciamento di una fermata programmata, guasti dell'impianto), sia di altra natura (scioperi o revoche degli stessi, problemi relativi al combustibile, eventi naturali). Variazione della disponibilità programmata: Variazione programmata della potenza che un'unità di produzione può erogare.

SECTION: Ruoli e Responsabilità - Funzioni della Divisione Midstream
ID: 17
CONTENT:
Compliance & Business Support (C&BS): Funzione della Direzione Market Design, Compliance & Business Support che ha il compito di gestire e coordinare le attività di compliance della Divisione Midstream. Ricopre il ruolo di indirizzo delle attività di compliance al REMIT nell'ambito del Gruppo Edison. Direzione Portfolio Analysis, Forecasting & Operations: Direzione della Business Unit Gas Supply, Portfolio Management & Logistics che fornisce il supporto alla pubblicazione delle Informazioni Privilegiate legate alla commodity gas e alle attività di reporting dei Fundamental Data.

SECTION: Funzioni Operative - Gas Operations e Portfolio Management
ID: 18
CONTENT:
Gas Operations & Balancing: Funzione della Direzione Portfolio Analysis, Forecasting & Operations responsabile dell'esecuzione delle attività di pubblicazione relative alle informazioni inerenti alla commodity gas. ID: 26
CONTENT:
Nel presente documento vengono definite le attività, i ruoli e le responsabilità previste per l'assolvimento agli obblighi definiti nel Regolamento REMIT, in conseguenza alle attività svolte dalla Divisione Midstream e della responsabilità di supporto e indirizzo per le attività di tutte le strutture del Gruppo Edison in ambito di compliance REMIT e MAR assegnata alla Divisione stessa. SECTION: Supporto della Funzione C&BS per la Compliance REMIT
ID: 27
CONTENT:
La Funzione C&BS fornisce supporto per quanto riguarda: la definizione delle pratiche operative da adottare ai fini della compliance al Regolamento REMIT, la verifica delle soluzioni operative adottate dalle strutture del Gruppo, la valutazione dei rischi di compliance pertinenti, lo sviluppo di interventi formativi, ed è il riferimento per le diverse strutture Edison sui Regolamenti. Al fine di garantire una gestione completa e coerente della compliance nella Divisione Midstream, la Funzione C&BS si avvale del supporto di "Focal Point di Divisione" individuati nelle Unità Organizzative di Divisione.

CONTENT:

text:
DOCUMENT: Edison Compliance agli obblighi del regolamento REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Responsabilità della Funzione C&BS per l'Aggiornamento del Registro REMIT
ID: 30
CONTENT:
La Funzione C&BS, come descritto nell'Allegato VIII della Policy Commodity Market Abuse N.G. 09/18, in seguito alle segnalazioni ricevute dalla Direzione Corporate Affairs o qualora venga a conoscenza di cambiamenti societari intercorsi per mezzo di altri canali ufficiali, è responsabile di: a) Verificare se la segnalazione sia rilevante al fine dell'aggiornamento del Registro REMIT e aggiornare di conseguenza il DB REMIT; b) Segnalare agli Amministratori Delegati delle società controllate di Edison S.p.A. la necessità di procedere con l'iscrizione della società di propria competenza all'interno del Registro REMIT o, qualora questa sia già registrata, procedere con l'aggiornamento dei relativi dati, secondo le modalità descritte nel 'Manuale di funzionamento e uso del Registro REMIT' - RUM pubblicato e reso disponibile dall'Autorità di Regolazione per Energia Reti e Ambiente ARERA.

text:
DOCUMENT: Edison Compliance agli obblighi del regolamento REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Standard and Non-Standard Energy Contracts Classification
ID: 35
CONTENT:
In coerenza con quanto richiesto dall'obbligo normativo e con quanto espresso dalla European Federation of Energy Traders – EFET, il Gruppo Edison ha stabilito di considerare 'contratti standard' quei contratti caratterizzati da quantità determinate e prezzo fisso o prezzo indicizzato ad un unico indice semplice e 'contratti non standard' tutte le tipologie di contratto che non rientrano tra quelle descritte in precedenza. Un elenco esaustivo dei prodotti energetici all'ingrosso soggetti all'obbligo di reporting REMIT è fornito nell'Allegato II del presente documento (per maggiori approfondimenti si veda il Capitolo 2 della Policy Commodity Market Abuse di Gruppo). Si sottolinea che per le tipologie di contratto derivato che risultano essere soggette anche a reporting EMIR, l'obbligo di reporting è assolto riportando ai sensi EMIR in quanto il reporting dei contratti a fini EMIR ha anche valenza a fini REMIT.

text:
DOCUMENT: Edison Compliance agli obblighi del regolamento REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Settlement Function Responsibilities and Reporting Timelines
ID: 36
CONTENT:
Successivamente alla chiusura di contratti e/o all'inserimento in un Mercato Organizzato di ordini di compravendita su prodotti energetici all'ingrosso, indipendentemente dalla sede e dalle modalità di negoziazione ad opera delle Unità Organizzative della Divisione Midstream, la Funzione Settlement è incaricata della gestione operativa del reporting ai fini REMIT. In particolare, per le tipologie contrattuali standard, la Funzione Settlement è tenuta ad effettuare il reporting REMIT entro il giorno successivo alla negoziazione del contratto, mentre per le tipologie contrattuali non standard è tenuta ad effettuare il reporting entro 30 giorni dalla stipula del contratto; entro i medesimi termini devono essere segnalate eventuali modifiche del contratto (e.g. chiusura anticipata, novation, modifiche di prezzi e volumi) e in particolare per i contratti non standard, nel termine di 30 giorni dalla loro definizione, devono essere inoltre comunicati gli effettivi volumi consegnati / ritirati e il valore economico ad essi associato.

source: Edison Compliance agli obblighi del regolamento REMIT.pdf
text:
DOCUMENT: Edison Compliance agli obblighi del regolamento REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Organized Market Reporting Procedures
ID: 37
CONTENT:
In merito ai contratti e/o agli ordini di compravendita su prodotti energetici all'ingrosso negoziati su un Mercato Organizzato, le modalità di esecuzione del reporting utilizzate variano a seconda della rilevanza del mercato (e.g. GME) o del servizio di reporting messo a disposizione dal mercato stesso (e.g. EPEXSpot). Qualora il gestore di un mercato organizzato offra ai partecipanti di effettuare il servizio di reporting per loro conto attraverso l'RRM Equias, Edison incarica il gestore di effettuare il reporting per suo conto attraverso Equias, inviando il reporting sia dei contratti conclusi sia di tutti gli ordini inseriti da Edison sul mercato. La Funzione Settlement verifica la corretta esecuzione del reporting REMIT mediante l'accesso quotidiano ad Equias e il controllo della corrispondenza dei contratti riportati dal gestore con quanto registrato in OpenLink o in altri sistemi aziendali gestendo eventuali difformità rilevate e archiviando l'esito dei controlli effettuati.

text:
DOCUMENT: Edison Compliance agli obblighi del regolamento REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Alternative RRM Providers and Manual Data Upload Procedures
ID: 38
CONTENT:
Qualora il gestore di un mercato organizzato offra ai partecipanti di effettuare il servizio di reporting per loro conto attraverso un RRM diverso da Equias, Edison valutato l'RRM proposto dal gestore del mercato e ritenutolo accettabile, incarica il gestore di effettuare il reporting per suo conto attraverso quest'ultimo. Qualora non si procedesse ad incaricare l'RRM proposto si veda quanto previsto al punto successivo. La Funzione Settlement verifica quotidianamente la corretta esecuzione del reporting REMIT accedendo alla piattaforma del gestore del mercato verificando la corrispondenza dei contratti riportati dal gestore con quanto registrato in OpenLink o in altri sistemi aziendali e archiviando le evidenze dei controlli effettuati. Nel caso in cui il gestore non offra ai partecipanti di effettuare il servizio di reporting per loro conto, il gestore ha comunque l'obbligo di rendere disponibili (in modalità e formati che possono variare da mercato a mercato) i dati relativi alle operazioni eseguite; la Funzione Settlement procede quotidianamente a scaricare manualmente i dati delle transazioni e degli ordini effettuati in formato XML, come resi disponibili dal gestore del mercato, e a caricarli su Equias, che a sua volta li trasmette ad ACER ai fini del reporting REMIT.
