text:
DOCUMENT: Edison Policy Commodity Market Abuse.pdf
SECTION: Abusive Squeeze (Market Cornering) - Descrizione ed Esemplificazione
ID: 158
CONTENT:
La fattispecie Abusive Squeeze, in coerenza con la definizione fornita, prevede che i soggetti che hanno una significativa influenza sulla domanda, sull'offerta o sulla consegna di un prodotto abusino della loro posizione dominante sul mercato al fine di distorcere significativamente il prezzo al quale altri operatori, relativamente allo stesso prodotto, sono obbligati ad assolvere i loro impegni. Esempi significativi ma non esaustivi inerenti la fattispecie Abusive Squeeze possono configurarsi qualora un Operatore di Mercato agisca abbassando volontariamente i prezzi dell'energia elettrica in una zona in cui si configura come dominante nell'ottica di sfavorire i contratti di vendita di energia elettrica sottoscritti dai propri competitors abbassandone indirettamente il prezzo. Tale fattispecie si può realizzare qualora l'Operatore di Mercato eserciti un'influenza significativa in termini di posizioni di acquisto o vendita in un mercato. In particolare, la fattispecie Abusive Squeeze si può configurare abusando della propria posizione dominante nel mercato elettrico spot (mercato zonale) qualora le centrali di produzione si trovino in zone con limitazioni di trasporto elettrico.

text:
DOCUMENT: Edison Policy Commodity Market Abuse.pdf
SECTION: Cross-market Manipulation - Definizione
ID: 159
CONTENT:
Cross-market manipulation: 'Trading on one market to improperly position the price of a wholesale energy product on a related market. This practice involves undertaking trading in one market with a view to improperly influencing the price of the same or a related wholesale energy product in another market'

metadata.title: Cross-market Manipulation - Definizione
metadata.original_text: Cross-market manipulation: 'Trading on one market to improperly position the price of a wholesale energy product on a related market. This practice involves undertaking trading in one market with a view to improperly influencing the price of the same or a related wholesale energy product in another market'

text:
DOCUMENT: Edison Policy Commodity Market Abuse.pdf
SECTION: Cross-market Manipulation - Descrizione ed Esemplificazione
ID: 160
CONTENT:
La fattispecie Cross-market manipulation si caratterizza per il tentativo di manipolare il prezzo di un prodotto in un mercato al fine di manipolare il prezzo dello stesso o di un prodotto differente su un altro mercato ad esso correlato. Tale fattispecie si può configurare mediante l'esecuzione di operazioni finalizzate a comportare la variazione del prezzo di un prodotto su un mercato che comporta un effetto (solitamente più rilevante) sul prezzo di un altro prodotto su un mercato correlato. La casistica maggiormente verosimile per la manifestazione della fattispecie in esame è rappresentata dall'esecuzione di specifiche operazioni sul mercato del gas finalizzate a conseguire benefici sul mercato del power. Un esempio di Cross-market manipulation si configura quando un Operatore di Mercato, al fine di ottenere posizioni lunghe/corte concernenti un prodotto del mercato Power, prende deliberatamente posizioni corte/lunghe su un mercato gas correlato, in ottica di portare i prezzi ad un valore favorevole.

SECTION: Prices not justified by market forces of supply and demand (Physical Withholding) - Definizione
ID: 161
CONTENT:
Prices not justified by market forces of supply and demand (physical withholding): 'Actions undertaken by persons that artificially cause prices to be at a level not justified by market forces of supply and demand, including actual availability in production, storage ore transportation capacity, and demand.'

text:
DOCUMENT: Edison Policy Commodity Market Abuse.pdf
SECTION: Prices not justified by market forces of supply and demand (Physical Withholding) - Descrizione ed Esemplificazione
ID: 162
CONTENT:
La fattispecie Prices not justified by market forces of supply and demand, in coerenza con la definizione fornita, è caratterizzata da un serie di azioni intraprese da un Operatore di Mercato ai fini di alzare o abbassare, indipendentemente dalle dinamiche di mercato, i prezzi nell'ottica di ottenere condizioni particolarmente favorevoli per la propria Società. La fattispecie, si configura quindi più facilmente per quegli operatori che hanno anche una posizione dominante nel mercato, e per tale motivazione si manifesta più facilmente sui mercati spot dell'energia elettrica e del gas naturale, in quanto gli operatori devono sottostare ai vincoli fisici imposti dai sistemi di trasmissione (e.g. rete elettrica, capacità) e produzione. In particolare, tale fattispecie può configurarsi ad esempio in un aumento/diminuzione anomalo del prezzo dell'energia elettrica in una determinata zona, dovuto alla mancata offerta, di un operatore, di tutta la potenza disponibile per la produzione di energia elettrica non giustificata da manutenzioni, guasti o altre motivazioni pertinenti. L'ARERA nella Delibera 111/06 ha espresso il concetto per cui gli operatori del mercato elettrico durante le fasi di pianificazione della produzione dei loro impianti sono tenuti ad agire secondo principi di diligenza, prudenza e competenza per non incorrere in possibili manipolazioni di mercato quali il 'Physical withholding'.

CONTENT:

text:
DOCUMENT: Edison Policy Commodity Market Abuse.pdf
SECTION: Pump and Dump - Definizione
ID: 165
CONTENT:
Pump and dump: 'This practice involves taking a long position in a wholesale energy product and then undertaking further buying activity and/or disseminating misleading positive information about the wholesale energy product with a view to increasing the price of the wholesale energy product. Other market participants are misled by the resulting effect on price and are attracted into purchasing the wholesale energy product. The manipulator then sells out at the inflated price.'

text:
DOCUMENT: Edison Policy Commodity Market Abuse.pdf
SECTION: Pump and Dump - Descrizione ed Esemplificazione
ID: 166
CONTENT:
La fattispecie Pump and dump consiste nel prendere una posizione lunga su un determinato prodotto, mettere in atto strategie di domanda volte a far incrementare il prezzo del prodotto per poi invertire la posizione. L'operatività analoga e opposta (i.e. adozione di una posizione corta su un prodotto e esecuzione di operazioni volte all'abbassamento del relativo prezzo) costituisce allo stesso modo manipolazione del mercato. Tale fattispecie solitamente è caratterizzata da un numero consistente di deal finalizzati a far incrementare/diminuire il prezzo del prodotto di interesse e dalla successiva repentina inversione di posizione su più volumi di quelli oggetto della posizione iniziale.

text:
DOCUMENT: Edison Policy Commodity Market Abuse.pdf
SECTION: Circular Trading and Pre-arranged Trading
ID: 169
CONTENT:
Circular trading prevede l'inserimento quasi simultaneo di due ordini uguali e opposti. Tale fattispecie si differenzia da quella denominata «Improper matched orders» in quanto presuppone che l'esecuzione di ordini simultanei uguali ed opposti sia effettuata dallo stesso operatore e non da due controparti in collusione. Molti mercati regolamentati prevedono segnalazioni automatiche in caso di inserimento di due ordini uguali e opposti da parte dello stesso operatore.

Pre-arranged trading è definito come "The practice of two commodity dealers trading with each other at prices upon which they have agreed in advance. Pre-arranged trading is designed to exclude other dealers from the market, to gain a tax advantage, or both". La fattispecie Pre-arranged trading è caratterizzata dall'esecuzione di una transazione su un prodotto negoziato tramite borsa per il quale i prezzi e le quantità sono state definite a priori tra le controparti. Le fattispecie Wash Trades e Improper Matched Orders costituiscono dei casi particolari di pre-arranged trading.

text:
DOCUMENT: Edison Policy Commodity Market Abuse.pdf
SECTION: Spreading False or Misleading Information
ID: 170
CONTENT:
Spreading false/misleading information through the media è definito come "This involves behavior such as posting information via internet or issuing a press release which contains false or misleading statements about a wholesale energy product which is admitted to trading on an organized market. The person spreading the information knows or ought to have known that it is false or misleading and is disseminating the information in order to create a false or misleading impression".

La fattispecie in questione prevede la diffusione di informazioni false o fuorvianti per mezzo dei canali di comunicazione al fine dare false impressioni agli altri Operatori di Mercato.

Other behavior designed to spread false/misleading information copre "a course of conduct designed to give a false and misleading impression through means other than the media. An example might be the movement of physical commodity stocks to create a misleading impression as to the supply or demand for a commodity or the deliverable into a commodity future contract". La fattispecie prevede la diffusione di informazioni false o fuorvianti per mezzo di canali diversi dai mezzi di comunicazione, quali ad esempio il trasferimento di quantitativi di gas stoccato, al fine dare false impressioni agli altri Operatori di Mercato.

text:
DOCUMENT: Edison Policy Commodity Market Abuse.pdf
SECTION: MAR Regulation Indicators for Market Manipulation Detection
ID: 171
CONTENT:
L'allegato I del Regolamento MAR definisce un set non esaustivo di indicatori da tenere in considerazione per l'identificazione di operazioni sospette di manipolazione di mercato. Tali indicatori possono fornire 'alert' in riferimento alla potenziale esecuzione di una delle tipologie di manipolazione di mercato.

Indicatori di manipolazioni consistenti nel fornire indicazioni false o fuorvianti e nel fissare i prezzi includono:

a) "The extent to which orders to trade given or transaction undertaken represent a significant proportion of the daily volume of transactions in the relevant financial instrument, related spot commodity contract, or auctioned product based on emission allowances, in particular when those activities lead to a significant change in their prices." Fattispecie correlate: Cross-market manipulation, Marking the Close.

b) "The extent to which orders to trade given or transactions undertaken by personas with a significant buying or selling position in a financial instrument, a related spot commodity contract, or an auctioned product based on emission allowances, lead to significant changes in the price of that financial instrument, related spot commodity contract, or auctioned product based on emission allowances." Fattispecie correlate: Abusive Squeeze, Cross-market manipulation.

text:
DOCUMENT: Edison Policy Commodity Market Abuse.pdf
SECTION: MAR Indicators - Beneficial Ownership and Position Reversals
ID: 172
CONTENT:
c) "Whether transactions undertaken lead to no change in beneficial ownership of a financial instrument, a related spot commodity contract, or an auctioned product based on emission allowances." Fattispecie correlate: Pre-arranged trading, Wash Trade, Improper Matched Orders, Placing Orders with no intention of executing them, Marking the Close.

d) "The extent to which orders to trade given or transactions undertaken or orders cancelled include position reversals in a short period and represent a significant proportion of the daily volume of transactions in the relevant financial instrument, a related spot commodity contract, or an auctioned product based on emission allowances, and might be associated with significant changes in the price of a financial instrument, a related spot commodity contract, or an auctioned product based on emission allowances." Fattispecie correlate: Pump and dump, Placing Orders with no intention of executing them.

d) "The extent to which orders to trade given or transactions undertaken or orders cancelled include position reversals in a short period and represent a significant proportion of the daily volume of transactions in the relevant financial instrument, a related spot commodity contract, or an auctioned product based on emission allowances, and might be associated with significant changes in the price of a financial instrument, a related spot commodity contract, or an auctioned product based on emission allowances." text:
DOCUMENT: Edison Policy Commodity Market Abuse.pdf
SECTION: MAR Indicators - Time Concentration and Order Book Manipulation
ID: 173
CONTENT:
e) "The extent to which orders to trade given or transactions undertaken are concentrated within a short time span in the trading session and lead to a price change which is subsequently reversed." Fattispecie correlate: Marking the Close, Placing Orders with no intention of executing them, Abusive Squeeze.

f) "The extent to which orders to trade given change the representation of the best bid or offer prices in a financial instrument, a related spot commodity contract, or an auctioned product based on emission allowances, or more generally the representation of the order book available to market participants and are removed before they are executed." Fattispecie correlate: Placing Orders with no intention of executing them, Cross-market manipulation, Prices not justified by market forces of supply and demand.

g) "The extent to which orders to trade are given or transactions are undertaken at or around a specific time when reference prices, settlement prices and valuations are calculated and lead to price changes which have an effect on such prices and valuations." Fattispecie correlate: Marking the Close, Cross-market manipulation.

text:
DOCUMENT: Edison Policy Commodity Market Abuse.pdf
SECTION: MAR Indicators - Fictitious Instruments and Deception
ID: 174
CONTENT:
Indicatori di manipolazioni consistenti nell'utilizzazione di strumenti fittizi o di altri tipi di inganno o espediente includono:

a) "Whether orders to trade given or transactions undertaken by personas are preceded or followed by dissemination of false or misleading information by the same persons or by persons linked to them." Fattispecie correlate: Dissemination of false or misleading market information through media, including the internet, or by any other means.

b) "Whether orders to trade are given or transactions are undertaken by persons before or after the same persons or persons linked to them produce or disseminate investment recommendations which are erroneous, biased, or demonstrably influenced by material interest." Fattispecie correlate: Spreading false/misleading information through the media.

text:
DOCUMENT: Edison Policy Commodity Market Abuse.pdf
SECTION: ALLEGATO VI - Template for Reporting Suspicious Market Abuse Operations
ID: 175
CONTENT:
La segnalazione di operazioni o comportamenti sospetti di abuso di informazioni privilegiate o di manipolazione del mercato deve avvenire mediante la redazione e trasmissione di un apposito report. Le segnalazioni trasmesse ai fini del Regolamento MAR devono contenere almeno le seguenti informazioni:

• Identificazione del soggetto che effettua la segnalazione e, nel caso in cui il segnalante predisponga o esegua a titolo professionale operazioni, indicazione dell'esecuzione di tali operazioni per proprio conto o per conto di terzi
• Descrizione dell'ordine o dell'operazione, indicando in particolare la tipologia dell'ordine/contratto, luogo dell'attività, prezzo e volume
• Motivi per cui si sospetta che l'ordine o l'operazione costituisca abuso di informazioni privilegiate, manipolazione di mercato ovvero tentato abuso di informazioni privilegiate o tentata manipolazione di mercato
• Mezzi per identificare le persone implicate nell'ordine o operazione oggetto della segnalazione e, in particolare, la persona che ha inoltrato o eseguito l'ordine e la persona per conto della quale l'ordine è stato inoltrato o eseguito
• Qualsiasi altra informazione e documento giustificativo considerati pertinenti per l'autorità competente ai fini dell'individuazione, investigazione e repressione dell'abuso di informazioni privilegiate, manipolazione di mercato ovvero tentato abuso di informazioni privilegiate o tentata manipolazione di mercato.

text:
DOCUMENT: Edison Policy Commodity Market Abuse.pdf
SECTION: REMIT Regulation Reporting Requirements
ID: 176
CONTENT:
Le segnalazioni trasmesse ai fini del Regolamento REMIT sono effettuate attraverso un template standard, disponibile al link: https://www.acer-remit.eu/np/str e devono contenere come best practice, per quanto definito dall'ACER, le seguenti informazioni:

• Tipologia di abuso del mercato: Insider trading e/o manipolazione del mercato e il loro dettaglio compresa l'identificazione della fattispecie di manipolazione del mercato
• Lo Stato o gli stati membri in cui è avvenuta la violazione e le relative Autorità competenti
• Informazioni di dettaglio relative a: nome, organizzazione, posizione e contatti del soggetto che esegue la segnalazione; informazioni relative a potenziali controparti interessate; descrizione della sospetta violazione.

ID: 2
CONTENT:
1.1 Scopo del documento: The document defines activities, roles and responsibilities for compliance with regulatory obligations introduced by EU Regulation No. 596/2014 (MAR - Market Abuse Regulation) related to derivatives on commodities and emission allowances to which Edison S.p.A., particularly the Gas Midstream Energy Management & Optimization Division, is subject. DOCUMENT: Edison Procedura MAR Quote Emissione.pdf
SECTION: 1.4 Roles and Responsibilities
ID: 3
CONTENT:
The following actors are involved in fulfilling MAR Regulation obligations: Funzione Compliance & Business Process Support (COMP) - manages and coordinates compliance activities of the Gas Midstream Energy Management & Optimization Division and supports Focal Points in defining and implementing compliance actions. Focal Point della Divisione - interfaces with COMP Function for operational compliance management activities delegated to Business Units and Divisions. Business Units e Direzioni della Divisione - operationally manage compliance activities with support from COMP Function when necessary. Direzioni e Funzioni Extra Divisione - support Organizational Units in operational management of compliance activities. Specifically: Direzione Internal Audit handles identification and reporting of suspicious transactions; Direzione Corporate Affairs handles identification and reporting of suspicious transactions and publication of privileged information related to emission allowances market.

ID: 6
CONTENT:
The document defines activities, roles and responsibilities for compliance with MAR Regulation obligations regarding derivatives on commodities and emission allowances within Edison S.p.A. text:
DOCUMENT: Edison Procedura MAR Quote Emissione.pdf
SECTION: 2.1 Obligation to Identify and Report Suspicious Transactions
ID: 7
CONTENT:
Actors involved: COMP and the Gas Midstream Energy Management & Optimization Division in its entirety, Internal Audit Direction. Process: The Gas Midstream Energy Management & Optimization Division has adopted an automatic monitoring system of transactions whose functionalities and methods satisfy requirements indicated in chapter 4.3.2 of the Group COMMODITY MARKET ABUSE Policy. The monitoring tool covers all trading activities carried out by Organizational Units of the Division falling within MAR Regulation scope and is constantly monitored by Division Focal Points who ensure timely notification of any variation in operational scope to COMP Function. Focal Points notify via email complianceG&P@edison.it any variations concerning: types of products traded by Business Units or Directions; place and methods of trading such products (Regulated Market, MTF system, OTF system or bilateral contracts).

SECTION: Monitoraggio automatico delle operazioni e analisi di mercato
ID: 10
CONTENT:
La Funzione COMP verifica se le eventuali variazioni nel perimetro di monitoraggio automatico siano rilevanti ai fini dello strumento di monitoraggio ed in tal caso provvede conseguentemente a richiedere l'aggiornamento del sistema di monitoraggio e a calibrare le relative soglie necessarie alle analisi stesse. In coerenza con quanto definito nel Capitolo 4.3.2 della Policy COMMODITY MARKET ABUSE di Gruppo, le operazioni identificate dal sistema di monitoraggio automatico come potenzialmente sospette di abuso del mercato vengono sottoposte a analisi e verifiche approfondite ad opera della Funzione COMP.

text:
DOCUMENT: Edison Procedura MAR Quote Emissione.pdf
SECTION: Verifiche della Funzione COMP su operazioni sospette - Step 1 e 2
ID: 11
CONTENT:
In particolare, la Funzione COMP esegue le verifiche necessarie utilizzando livelli di approfondimento differenti: 1. Come primo step la Funzione COMP verifica, anche mediante il confronto con eventuali analisi precedentemente svolte, che le operazioni sospette riscontrate non siano falsi positivi dovuti alla taratura di eventuali soglie del sistema di monitoraggio e, nel caso, provvede a ricalibrare opportunamente tali soglie; 2. Qualora le operazioni segnalate dal sistema come potenzialmente sospette non si rivelino falsi positivi, la Funzione COMP effettua per conto proprio un approfondimento di tali operazioni, tenendo in considerazione le condizioni e l'andamento dei mercati ad esse associati.

ID: 12
CONTENT:

CONTENT:
Nel caso in cui a seguito degli approfondimenti svolti, la Funzione COMP non abbia identificato le motivazioni che giustifichino l'esecuzione delle operazioni sospette, qualora non ritenga che il Direttore della Business Unit o Direzione di competenza abbia avuto responsabilità nell'esecuzione di tali operazioni, comunica le operazioni in questione al Direttore della Business Unit o Direzione di competenza e provvede ad analizzare i casi sospetti mediante il suo supporto. In seguito alle analisi effettuate: i.) Nel caso in cui siano state identificate opportune motivazioni, la Funzione COMP e il Direttore della Business Unit o Direzione di competenza provvedono a segnalare, a fini formativi, tali le operazioni al personale attivo sui mercati.

text:
DOCUMENT: Edison Procedura MAR Quote Emissione.pdf
SECTION: Segnalazione all'Autorità competente per abuso di mercato
ID: 14
CONTENT:
Nel caso in cui non siano state identificate motivazioni che giustifichino l'esecuzione delle operazioni sospette, la Funzione COMP, in concerto con il Direttore della Business Unit o della Direzione, provvedono ad informare la Direzione Internal Audit e il Direttore di Divisione. Successivamente la Funzione COMP, con il supporto della Direzione Corporate Affairs, procede con la segnalazione all'Autorità competente del potenziale abuso di mercato ai fini MAR, secondo le modalità previste dal processo definito nel Capitolo 4.3 della Policy COMMODITY MARKET ABUSE di Gruppo.

DOCUMENT: Edison Procedura MAR Quote Emissione.pdf
SECTION: Gestione operazioni sospette con responsabilità del Direttore
ID: 15
CONTENT:
Nel caso in cui a seguito degli approfondimenti svolti, la Funzione COMP non abbia identificato le motivazioni che giustifichino l'esecuzione delle operazioni sospette, qualora ritenga che il Direttore della Business Unit o Direzione di competenza abbia avuto responsabilità nell'esecuzione di tali operazioni, provvede a comunicare gli approfondimenti svolti per proprio conto alla Direzione Internal Audit. In seguito ad una analisi condivisa di tali operazioni, qualora non sia stata identificata alcuna motivazione per giustificare tale comportamento, la Funzione COMP in concerto con l'Internal Audit, provvede ad informare il Direttore di Divisione, qualora ritenga che il Direttore della Divisione non abbia avuto responsabilità nell'esecuzione di tali operazioni. Successivamente la Funzione COMP, con il supporto della Direzione Corporate Affairs, procede con la segnalazione all'Autorità competente del potenziale abuso di mercato ai fini MAR, secondo le modalità previste dal processo definito nel Capitolo 4.4 della Policy COMMODITY MARKET ABUSE di Gruppo.

text:
DOCUMENT: Edison Procedura MAR Quote Emissione.pdf
SECTION: Archiviazione e conservazione delle operazioni sospette
ID: 16
CONTENT:
La Funzione COMP archivia e conserva per un periodo minimo di cinque anni: • Gli ordini e le transazioni identificate come potenzialmente sospette di manipolazione di mercato, identificando in particolare per ogni operazione sospetta il prodotto considerato e la data della potenziale manipolazione; • Le condizioni di mercato nel quale tali operazioni e transazioni hanno avuto luogo (e.g. presenza di informazioni privilegiate, chiusura del mercato, settlement di un derivato); • Le modalità e le informazioni utilizzate per le analisi, con particolare riferimento alla data di inizio e fine degli approfondimenti necessari e agli attori coinvolti nel processo di analisi; • Le motivazioni che hanno portato alla giustificazione delle operazioni o transazioni sospette; • Altro, qualora lo ritenga rilevante.

CONTENT:

text:
DOCUMENT: Edison Procedura MAR Quote Emissione.pdf
SECTION: Istituzione e Composizione del Registro degli Insider
ID: 31
CONTENT:
Ogni qualvolta venga individuata una nuova informazione privilegiata connessa al mercato delle quote di emissione la Funzione COMP ha il compito di aggiungere al Registro degli Insider una nuova sezione. Il registro degli insider si compone della seguente sezione: I. sezione singolo evento – elenco suddiviso in sezioni distinte, una per ciascuna informazione privilegiata, in cui sono registrate le persone aventi accesso all'informazione privilegiata riferita al singolo evento a cui la sezione fa riferimento. In ciascuna sezione singolo evento possono essere iscritte le persone di seguito indicate qualora abbiano accesso a tale specifica informazione: • ogni soggetto interno - dipendenti e collaboratori - di Edison e delle società controllate; • i soggetti esterni che svolgono determinate funzioni in nome o per conto di Edison e delle società controllate in forza di uno specifico mandato.

text:
DOCUMENT: Edison Procedura MAR Quote Emissione.pdf
SECTION: Creazione della Sezione Singolo Evento e Informazioni Richieste
ID: 32
CONTENT:
La creazione di una sezione singolo evento nonché l'iscrizione dei nominativi delle persone che hanno accesso alla relativa informazione privilegiata, è tempestivamente effettuata dalla Funzione COMP sulla base della segnalazione ricevuta. Le informazioni ricevute sono eventualmente integrate con i dati forniti dalla direzione Human Resources ovvero dalle stesse persone iscritte. La segnalazione deve contenere le seguenti informazioni: a. la tipologia di informazione privilegiata comunicata o il suo nome in codice; b. l'identità delle persone che hanno avuto accesso a tale informazione: i. in caso di persona fisica: il nome, il cognome, la denominazione sociale della società di appartenenza, se diversa da Edison; ii. in caso di persona giuridica: la denominazione sociale nonché i dati di cui al precedente punto relativi a una persona di riferimento in grado di individuare (e iscrivere nel proprio registro degli insider) tutti coloro che all'interno della propria società/struttura hanno accesso all'informazione privilegiata.

text:
DOCUMENT: Edison Procedura MAR Quote Emissione.pdf
SECTION: Market Abuse Sanctions and Prohibited Conduct
ID: 57
CONTENT:
Regulations impose criminal and administrative sanctions for those possessing Privileged Information who use it to perform, directly or indirectly, modify or recommend operations on emission allowances (abuse of Privileged Information per art. 8 MAR), or communicate it to third parties without justified reason (unlawful communication per art. 10 MAR), or disseminate false information or conduct operations causing significant price alteration of financial instruments (market manipulation per art. 12 MAR). Prohibited: performing, modifying or recommending operations on financial instruments based on Privileged Information until such information is made public. Applicable sanctions include: criminal penalties, accessory penalties, confiscation of proceeds or profits, administrative sanctions including pecuniary sanctions, temporary or permanent interdiction from functions, and restitution of gains realized or losses avoided through violation. EDISON reserves right to recover damages and may terminate employment/collaboration for just cause without notice for violations.

COMMISSION IMPLEMENTING REGULATION (EU) No 1348/2014 of 17 December 2014 on data reporting implementing Article 8(2) and Article 8(6) of Regulation (EU) No 1227/2011 of the European Parliament and of the Council on wholesale energy market integrity and transparency. THE EUROPEAN COMMISSION, Having regard to the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, Having regard to Regulation (EU) No 1227/2011 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 25 October 2011 on wholesale energy market integrity and transparency, and in particular Article 8(2) and Article 8(6) thereof.

THE EUROPEAN COMMISSION, Having regard to the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, Having regard to Regulation (EU) No 1227/2011 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 25 October 2011 on wholesale energy market integrity and transparency, and in particular Article 8(2) and Article 8(6) thereof.

text:
DOCUMENT: Implementing Regulation.pdf
SECTION: Recitals 1-3: Market Oversight and Reporting Requirements
ID: 1
CONTENT:
Effective oversight of wholesale energy markets requires the regular monitoring of details of contracts including orders to trade as well as data on capacity and use of facilities for production, storage, consumption or transmission of electricity and natural gas. Regulation (EU) No 1227/2011 requires the Agency for the Cooperation of Energy Regulators (the Agency) established by Regulation (EC) No 713/2009 to monitor wholesale energy markets in the Union. In order to enable the Agency to fulfil its task it should be provided with complete sets of relevant information in a timely manner. Market participants should report to the Agency on a regular basis details of wholesale energy contracts both in relation to the supply of electricity and natural gas and for the transportation of those commodities. Contracts for balancing services, contracts between different members of the same group of companies and contracts for the sale of the output of small energy production facilities should be reported to the Agency only at its reasoned request on ad-hoc basis.

text:
DOCUMENT: Implementing Regulation.pdf
SECTION: Recitals 4-6: Reporting Parties, Data Collection, and Derivatives
ID: 2
CONTENT:
In general, both parties to the contract should report the required details of the concluded contract. To facilitate reporting, parties should be able to report on each other's behalf or use the services of third parties for this purpose. The details of transportation contracts acquired through primary capacity allocation of a transmission system operator (TSO) should be reported by the respective TSO only. The reported data should also include filled and unfilled capacity requests. In order to effectively uncover market abuses, the Agency can monitor orders to trade placed on organised markets. Matched and unmatched orders should be reported through the organised market place where they were placed or through third parties who are able to provide such information. In order to avoid double reporting, the Agency should collect details of derivatives relating to contracts for the supply or transportation of electricity or natural gas which have been reported in accordance with applicable financial regulation to trade repositories or to financial regulators from those sources.

text:
DOCUMENT: Implementing Regulation.pdf
SECTION: Recitals 7-9: Standard vs Non-Standard Contracts and User Guidance
ID: 3
CONTENT:
Efficient reporting and targeted monitoring requires standard and non-standard contracts to be distinguished. Since prices of standard contracts serve also as reference prices for non-standard contracts, the Agency should receive information regarding standard contracts on a daily basis. Details of non-standard contracts should be reportable up to one month from their conclusion. It is important that reporting parties have a clear understanding about the details of the information they are required to report. To this end the Agency should explain the content of the reportable information in a user manual. The Agency should also make sure that information is reported in electronic formats, which are easily accessible to reporting parties.

text:
DOCUMENT: Implementing Regulation.pdf
SECTION: Recitals 10-12: Data Transfer Requirements and Phased Implementation
ID: 4
CONTENT:
In order to ensure continuous and safe transfer of complete sets of data, the reporting parties should comply with basic requirements in relation to their ability to authenticate data sources, check data for correctness and completeness and to ensure business continuity. The Agency should assess reporting parties' compliance with those requirements. The obligation for reporting should be phased in, starting with transmitting fundamental data available on the transparency platforms of ENTSO for Electricity and of ENTSO for Gas as well as standard contracts executed at organised market places. Reporting of non-standard contracts should follow reflecting the extra time needed for completing procedures for reporting. The measures provided for in this Regulation are in accordance with the opinion of the Committee established in accordance with Article 21 of Regulation (EU) No 1227/2011.

text:
DOCUMENT: Implementing Regulation.pdf
SECTION: Chapter I: General Provisions - Articles 1-2
ID: 5
CONTENT:
Article 1 Subject matter: This Regulation lays down rules for the provision of data to the Agency implementing Article 8(2) and (6) of Regulation (EU) No 1227/2011. It defines the details of reportable wholesale energy products and fundamental data. It also establishes appropriate channels for data reporting including defining timing and regularity of data reports. Article 2 Definitions: For the purpose of this Regulation, the definitions in Article 2 of Regulation (EU) No 1227/2011 and in Article 3 of Commission Regulation (EU) No 984/2013 shall apply.

text:
DOCUMENT: Implementing Regulation.pdf
SECTION: Article 2 Definitions (1-7): Fundamental Data, Contracts, and Market Types
ID: 6
CONTENT:
'Fundamental data' means information related to the capacity and use of facilities for production, storage, consumption or transmission of electricity and natural gas or related to the capacity and use of LNG facilities, including planned or unplanned unavailability of these facilities. 'Standard contract' means a contract concerning a wholesale energy product admitted to trading at an organised market place, irrespective of whether or not the transaction actually takes place on that market place. 'Non-standard contract' means a contract concerning any wholesale energy product that is not a standard contract. 'Organised market place' or 'organised market' means a multilateral system which brings together or facilitates the bringing together of multiple third party buying and selling interests in wholesale energy products in a way that results in a contract, or any other system or facility in which multiple third-party buying and selling interests in wholesale energy products are able to interact in a way that results in a contract. These include electricity and gas exchanges, brokers and other persons professionally arranging transactions, and trading venues as defined in Article 4 of Directive 2014/65/EU.

text:
DOCUMENT: Implementing Regulation.pdf
SECTION: Article 2 Definitions (8-13): Groups, OTC, Nominations, and Balancing
ID: 7
CONTENT:
'Group' shall have the same meaning as in Article 2 of Directive 2013/34/EU. 'Intragroup contract' is a contract on wholesale energy products entered into with a counterparty which is part of the same group provided that both counterparties are included in the same consolidation on a full basis. 'Over-the-counter' (OTC) means any transaction carried out outside an organised market. 'Nomination' means for electricity: the notification of the use of cross zonal capacity by a physical transmission rights holder and its counterparty to the respective transmission system operator(s)(TSOs), and for natural gas: the prior reporting by the network user to the TSO of the actual flow that the network user wishes to inject into or withdraw from the system. 'Balancing energy' means energy used by TSOs to perform balancing. 'Balancing capacity (reserves)' means the contracted reserve capacity. 'Balancing services' means for electricity: either or both balancing capacity and balancing energy, and for natural gas: a service provided to a TSO via a contract for gas required to meet short term fluctuations in gas demand or supply. 'Consumption unit' means a resource which receives electricity or natural gas for its own use. 'Production unit' means a facility for generation of electricity made up of a single generation unit or of an aggregation of generation units.

DOCUMENT: Implementing Regulation.pdf
SECTION: Chapter II: Article 3 - List of Reportable Contracts (Part 1)

SECTION: Wholesale Energy Products - Supply Contracts
ID: 10
CONTENT:
Wholesale energy products in relation to the supply of electricity or natural gas in the Union include: Contracts relating to electricity or natural gas produced, traded or delivered in the Union between two or more parties, concluded as a result of a primary explicit auction or a secondary market concluded between market participants, specifying physical or financial energy rights or obligations. This includes contracts for a single consumption unit with technical capability to consume 600 GWh/year or more. Options, futures, swaps and any other derivatives of contracts relating to electricity or natural gas produced, traded or delivered in the Union are also included.

Options, futures, swaps and any other derivatives of contracts relating to the transportation of electricity or natural gas in the Union are also included.

SECTION: Agency Obligations for Standard Contracts and Organised Market Places
ID: 12
CONTENT:
In order to facilitate reporting, the Agency shall draw up and maintain a public list of standard contracts and update that list in a timely manner. The Agency shall draw up and publish a list of organised market places upon entry into force of this regulation and update that list in a timely manner. Organised market places shall submit identifying reference data for each wholesale energy product they admit to trading to the Agency before trading commences in that particular contract, in a format defined by the Agency. Organised market places shall submit updates of the information as changes occur. Final customers party to a contract shall inform their counterparty about the technical capability of the consumption unit in question to consume 600 GWh/year or more.

SECTION: Timing of Reporting for Standard Contracts and Orders
ID: 18
CONTENT:
Details of standard contracts and orders to trade, including for auctions, shall be reported as soon as possible but no later than on the working day following the conclusion of the contract or placement of the order. Any modification or the termination of the concluded contract or order to trade shall be reported as soon as possible but no later than the working day following the modification or termination. In the case of auction markets where orders are not made publicly visible, only concluded contracts and final orders shall be reported no later than on the working day following the auction. Orders placed in brokers' voice operated services and not appearing on electronic screens shall be reportable only upon request of the Agency.

SECTION: LNG System Operators - Reporting Requirements
ID: 24
CONTENT:
LNG system operators as defined in Article 2(12) of Directive 2009/73/EC shall report to the Agency and, at their request, to national regulatory authorities for each LNG facility the following information: (a) the technical, contracted and available capacity of the LNG facility in a daily resolution, (b) send-out and inventory of the LNG facility in a daily resolution, (c) planned and unplanned unavailability announcements of the LNG facility including the time of the announcement and the capacities concerned. The information including updates of it referred to in point (c) shall be made available as soon as that information becomes available.

SECTION: Article 11 - Technical and Organisational Requirements
ID: 29
CONTENT:
In order to ensure efficient, effective and safe exchange and handling of information, the Agency shall, after consulting relevant parties, develop technical and organisational requirements for submitting data. The Agency shall consult relevant parties on material updates of these requirements. The requirements shall: (a) ensure the security, confidentiality and completeness of information, (b) enable the identification and correction of errors in data reports, (c) enable the authentication of the source of information, (d) ensure business continuity. The Agency shall assess whether reporting parties comply with the requirements. Reporting parties who comply with the requirements shall be registered by the Agency. For entities listed under Article 6(4) the requirements listed in the second subparagraph shall be considered as fulfilled.

Persons required to report data referred to in Articles 6, 8 and 9 shall have responsibility for the completeness, accuracy and timely submission of data to the Agency and, where required so, to national regulatory authorities. In those cases the third party shall be responsible for those failures, without prejudice to Articles 4 and 18 of Regulation (EC) No 543/2013 on submission of data in electricity markets. Persons referred to in the first subparagraph shall nevertheless take reasonable steps to verify the completeness, accuracy and timeliness of the data which they submit through third parties.

ID: 31
CONTENT:
This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union. The reporting obligation as provided in Article 9(1) shall apply from 7 October 2015. The reporting obligation as provided in Article 6(1) except in relation to contracts referred to in Article 3(1)(b) shall apply from 7 October 2015. The reporting obligations as provided in Article 8(1) shall apply from 7 October 2015 but not before the central information transparency platform becomes operational pursuant to Article 3(3) of Regulation (EU) No 543/2013. The reporting obligations as provided in Articles 6(2), 6(3), 8(3), 9(2), 9(3), 9(5), 9(7) and 9(9) shall apply from 7 April 2016. The reporting obligation as provided in Article 6(1) in relation to contracts referred to in Article 3(1)(b) shall apply from 7 April 2016. Without prejudice to the second and fifth subparagraphs of paragraph 2 the Agency may enter into agreements with organised marketplaces, trade matching or reporting systems to obtain details of contracts before the reporting obligation becomes applicable.

European Commission public consultation on Commission Decision (EU) 2020/2152 on REMIT Fees. Submission by Elettricità Futura & Proxigas on 26th November 2024. text:
DOCUMENT: Proxigas REMIT Fees Elettricità Futura.pdf
SECTION: Experience with Fee Decision and Implementation Issues
ID: 1
CONTENT:
Elettricità Futura and Proxigas acknowledge the significant increase of data reported and evolution of the scope of data reporting obligations under REMIT II. Costs for implementing REMIT have risen considerably between 2021 and 2024. However, Market Participants lack information about cost breakdowns including wages, consultancy services, IT and ICT costs, and events. ACER has not provided forecasts per REMIT activities or cost categories. The organizations invite ACER to publish a mid-term forward-looking budget related to REMIT with breakdown per category and activities, including information about the Commission's financial contribution to ACER activities.

text:
DOCUMENT: Proxigas REMIT Fees Elettricità Futura.pdf
SECTION: Non-Discriminatory Approach to REMIT Fees
ID: 2
CONTENT:
While the current implementation of the Fee Decision is generally favourable, a stricter non-discriminatory approach to REMIT fees is essential and should be strengthened in the next Fee Decision. This should consider smaller entities that report limited numbers of transactions, such as small Market Participants, storage operators, small producers, and non-commercial Registered Reporting Mechanisms (RRMs). The 'enrolment fee' should be standardized for all group entities liable for fee payments, maintaining parity for both RRMs and Inside Information Platforms (IIPs). The 'supervisory fee' should be proportional to the number of records submitted rather than uniform for all RRMs, as supervisory effort is directly correlated with the volume of records received by ACER.

text:
DOCUMENT: Proxigas REMIT Fees Elettricità Futura.pdf
SECTION: Issues with Multiple Reporting Activities and Over-Invoicing
ID: 3
CONTENT:
When a market participant reports on behalf of others, this reporting is considered as an additional data cluster, leading to additional variable cluster fees. When MPs have delegated reporting to other MPs through a commercial RRM, each MP is charged a separate cluster for reporting 'on behalf of', resulting in over-invoicing. The reporting party incurs higher costs than if transactions were considered as part of a single reporting cluster, since costs per transaction decrease with volume. This effect is amplified when reporting on behalf occurs in different transaction groups (EMIR transactions, Direct electronic access transactions, etc.), leading to multiplication of separate data clusters.

text:
DOCUMENT: Proxigas REMIT Fees Elettricità Futura.pdf
SECTION: Proposed Solution for Multiple Reporting
ID: 4
CONTENT:
Transactions reported on behalf of another MP should be integrated into the reporting MPs' existing clusters, while increasing fees for existing clusters by the necessary amount to reach expected total REMIT fees per year. This measure would ensure RRM/ACER costs are covered while reducing over-invoicing potential and significantly reducing administrative burden due to the limited number of MPs subject to REMIT fees. Additional ACER guidance to commercial RRMs is essential. Reporting on behalf of other MPs enables increased transparency in the energy market and allows smaller MPs with limited resources to comply with REMIT obligations.

text:
DOCUMENT: Proxigas REMIT Fees Elettricità Futura.pdf
SECTION: Proposals for Inside Information Platforms (IIPs) Fees
ID: 5
CONTENT:
A uniform enrollment fee for IIPs fosters fairness, transparency, and predictability for all entities. Uniform fee structure ensures market participants, especially smaller entities, are not overwhelmed by excessive costs and preserves a level playing field by treating all entities equally. The proposal supports instituting solely annual fees, excluding any component based on transaction records. The enrolment fee for IIPs should be standardized and aligned with that for RRMs and should not exceed 15,000 EUR per year. No variable fee component like records-based fees should apply to transaction reporting for urgent market messages (UMMs), consistent with their informative nature.

text:
DOCUMENT: Proxigas REMIT Fees Elettricità Futura.pdf
SECTION: Rationale Against Variable Fees for UMMs
ID: 6
CONTENT:
A variable fee component for urgent market messages could compromise transparency and the well-functioning of the market, creating uncertainty and cost unpredictability. This would make it challenging for IIPs to foresee and manage their regulatory obligations. Therefore, the proposal supports the European Commission's position not to apply variable fee components to UMM transaction reporting.

Therefore, the proposal supports the European Commission's position not to apply variable fee components to UMM transaction reporting.

SECTION: Supervisory Fee Component and Cost Coverage
ID: 9
CONTENT:
The 'supervision fee' is consistent with ACER's new supervisory powers over RRMs and IIPs. Following the principle of proportionality, the supervisory fee should be proportional to the average number of reports submitted rather than uniform for all, given that ACER's supervisory effort is directly dependent on the volume of reports received. The supervisory burden and associated costs are more substantial for commercial RRMs/IIPs managing records for hundreds or thousands of Market Participants, consequently requiring higher surveillance burden and related costs from ACER.

DOCUMENT: Proxigas REMIT Fees Elettricità Futura.pdf
SECTION: Cost Increases Due to Inflation
ID: 10
CONTENT:
Simple correction mechanisms are recommended rather than complex ones based on historical figures. To reduce system burden at RRMs billing systems level, continuous review should be avoided and only 5-year reviews should be planned. The total amount of the fee should be defined at a value equal to the current annual requirement plus the estimated rate of inflation for the next five years. The existing 'reduction amount' mechanism should be employed during the five years to adjust ACER's specific yearly needs to the collected fees.

DOCUMENT: Regulation amending REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Recital 1 - Market Integrity and Transparency Objectives
ID: 1
CONTENT:
Open and fair competition in the internal markets for electricity and for gas and ensuring a level playing field for market participants requires integrity and transparency of wholesale energy markets. Regulation (EU) No 1227/2011 of the European Parliament and of the Council establishes a comprehensive framework to achieve that objective. To enhance the public's trust in functioning wholesale energy markets and to protect the Union effectively against market abuse, Regulation (EU) No 1227/2011 should be amended to ensure further transparency and increase monitoring capacities, thereby contributing to the stabilisation of energy prices and consumer protection, as well as to ensure more effective investigation and enforcement of cases of potential cross-border market abuse addressing the shortcomings identified in the current framework.

DOCUMENT: Regulation amending REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Recital 2 - Market Manipulation Definition and Financial Instruments Alignment
ID: 2
CONTENT:
Financial instruments, including energy derivatives, traded on wholesale energy markets are of increasing importance. Due to the increasingly close interrelation between financial markets and wholesale energy markets, Regulation (EU) No 1227/2011 should be better aligned with the financial market legislation of the Union, such as Regulation (EU) No 596/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council, including with respect to the definitions of market manipulation and inside information. The definition of market manipulation in Regulation (EU) No 1227/2011 should therefore be amended to align it with Article 12 of Regulation (EU) No 596/2014. The definition should be amended to capture the entering into any transaction, or issuing, modifying or withdrawing any order to trade, but also any other behaviour relating to wholesale energy products which gives, or is likely to give, false or misleading signals as to the supply of, demand for, or price of wholesale energy products; secures, or is likely to secure, by a person, or persons acting in collaboration, the price of one or more wholesale energy products at an artificial level; or employs a fictitious device or any other form of deception or contrivance which gives, or is likely to give, false or misleading signals regarding the supply of, demand for, or price of wholesale energy products. The notion of any other behaviour relating to wholesale energy products should include, but should not be limited to, actions such as quote stuffing, painting the tape or momentum ignition.

DOCUMENT: Regulation amending REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Recital 3 - Inside Information Definition and Staged Processes
ID: 3
CONTENT:
The definition of inside information should be amended to align it with Regulation (EU) No 596/2014. In particular, where inside information concerns a process which occurs in stages, each stage of the process as well as the overall process could constitute inside information. An intermediate step in a protracted process could in itself constitute a set of particular circumstances or a particular event which exists or where there is a realistic prospect that they will come into existence or occur, on the basis of an overall assessment of the factors existing at the relevant time. However, that should not be interpreted as meaning that the magnitude of the effect of that set of circumstances or that event on the prices of the wholesale energy products concerned is to be taken into consideration. An intermediate step in a protracted process should be considered to be inside information if it, by itself, meets the criteria laid down in this Regulation for inside information.

SECTION: Recital 6 - Agency Publication of Non-Sensitive Information
ID: 6
CONTENT:
Where information shared with the European Agency for the Cooperation of Energy Regulators (the 'Agency') is not, or is no longer, sensitive from a commercial or security point of view, the Agency should be able to make that information available to market participants and to the wider public in an accessible manner with a view to contributing to enhanced knowledge about the wholesale energy markets. This should include the possibility for the Agency to publish aggregated information on organised marketplaces (OMPs), inside information platforms (IIPs) and registered reporting mechanisms (RRMs) in accordance with applicable data protection law with the aim of improving transparency of wholesale energy markets and provided that it does not distort competition on those energy markets.

SECTION: Recital 7 - Agency Trade Database for Scientific Purposes
ID: 7
CONTENT:
Where information shared with the Agency is not, or is no longer, sensitive from a commercial point of view, the Agency should be able to make its commercially non-sensitive trade database available for scientific purposes, subject to confidentiality requirements, with a view to contributing to enhanced knowledge about the wholesale energy markets. This is intended to help to build confidence in, and to foster the development of knowledge about, the functioning of wholesale energy markets. The Agency should establish and make publicly available rules on how it intends to make the information available for scientific and transparency purposes in a fair and transparent manner.

SECTION: Recital 8 - Digital Reference Centre for Union Wholesale Energy Market Data
ID: 8
CONTENT:
In order to further enhance market transparency in the Union wholesale energy markets and to contribute to a common Union energy data strategy, the Agency should develop and maintain a digital reference centre containing information on Union wholesale energy market data (the 'Reference Centre'). The Agency should make public, in a user-friendly manner, parts of the information which it collects pursuant to this Regulation, including information regarding the trading of over-the-counter wholesale energy contracts, power purchase agreements and contracts for difference. Any data made public by means of the Reference Centre should be subject to this Regulation and to the applicable data protection law.

ID: 11
CONTENT:
Compliance with the reporting obligations under Regulation (EU) No 1227/2011 and the quality of the data that the Agency receives is of the utmost importance in order to ensure the effective monitoring and detection of potential breaches with a view to achieving the objective of that Regulation. SECTION: Recital 12 - Expanded Data Collection and Order Book Requirements
ID: 12
CONTENT:
In order to improve the Agency's wholesale energy market monitoring and make data collection more complete, the current reporting regime needs improvement. The data collected should be expanded to overcome gaps in the data collection and should include coupled markets, new balancing markets, contracts for balancing markets, allocated transmission capacities and products that have potential delivery in the Union. OMPs should be required to make available to the Agency data relating to the order book or, upon request, provide the Agency with access, without delay, to the order book. Order book providers should also be designated as persons professionally arranging transactions subject to the obligation to monitor and report suspected breaches of this Regulation.

SECTION: Recital 15 - Inside Information Platforms Authorization and Requirements
ID: 15
CONTENT:
IIPs should play an important role for the effective disclosure of inside information. It should be mandatory to disclose inside information on dedicated IIPs to make the information easily accessible and to enhance transparency. Market participants may, only in addition, continue to use other channels, including market participants' websites, to disclose inside information. To ensure trust in the IIPs, they should be authorised pursuant to this Regulation. IIPs, including those registered by the Agency pursuant to Article 11 of Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) No 1348/2014, should comply with the requirements for authorisation and with data protection law. The Agency should have the power to withdraw such authorisation in certain cases, while respecting the procedural safeguards referred to in Article 14(6), (7) and (8) of Regulation (EU) 2019/942 of the European Parliament and of the Council. The withdrawal of an authorisation should not prevent an entity from applying for a new authorisation as IIP with the Agency. IIPs registered by the Agency pursuant to Implementing Regulation (EU) No 1348/2014 and included in the Agency's list of IIPs should be allowed to continue operating until the Agency has taken a decision on authorisation pursuant to this Regulation. IIPs should have mechanisms in place allowing inside information reports to be quickly and effectively checked. In the development of such mechanisms, IIPs may involve market participants.

SECTION: Inside Information Monitoring and Suspicious Transaction Reporting
ID: 18
CONTENT:
In order to facilitate monitoring to detect potential trading on the basis of inside information, the collection of inside information needs to be aligned with the current processes for trade data reporting. Persons professionally arranging or executing transactions should have the obligation to report suspicious transactions in breach of Regulation (EU) No 1227/2011 with regard to insider trading and market manipulation and, in order to enhance the possibility of enforcement of such breaches, should also have the obligation to report suspicious orders and potential breaches of the obligation to publish inside information. Direct electronic access providers and order book providers are considered to be persons professionally arranging transactions.

SECTION: Third-Country Participation in Union Electricity Coupling
ID: 19
CONTENT:
Commission Regulation (EU) 2015/1222 provides for the possibility for third-country participation in the Union single day-ahead and intraday coupling in the electricity sector. Since market-coupling operators use a specific algorithm to match bids and offers in an optimal manner, this may result in orders to trade being placed in a third country participating in the Union single day-ahead and intraday coupling but resulting in a contract for the supply of electricity with delivery in the Union. The placing of such orders to trade in third countries participating in the Union single day-ahead and intraday coupling that may result in delivery in the Union should be covered by the definition of wholesale energy products pursuant to this Regulation.

DOCUMENT: Regulation amending REMIT.pdf
SECTION: LNG Market Data Collection and Price Assessment
ID: 20
CONTENT:
In order to obtain an accurate, objective and reliable assessment of the price for liquefied natural gas (LNG) deliveries to the Union, the Agency should collect all the LNG market data that are necessary to establish a daily LNG price assessment and an LNG benchmark. The LNG price assessment and the LNG benchmark should be established on the basis of all transactions pertaining to LNG deliveries to the Union. The Agency should be empowered to collect the relevant market data from all participants active in LNG deliveries to the Union, which should report the LNG market data to the Agency as close to real time as technologically possible, either after the conclusion of a transaction or after the posting of a bid or offer to enter into a transaction. The Agency's LNG price assessment should comprise the most complete dataset including transaction prices, bids and offer prices for LNG deliveries to the Union. The daily publication of that objective LNG price assessment, and of the spread established in comparison to other reference prices on the market in the form of an LNG benchmark, paves the way for its voluntary uptake by market participants as the reference price in their contracts and transactions. Once established, the LNG price assessment and the LNG benchmark could also become a reference rate for derivative contracts used for hedging the price of LNG or the difference in price between the LNG price and other gas prices.

metadata.title: LNG Market Data Collection and Price Assessment
metadata.original_text: In order to obtain an accurate, objective and reliable assessment of the price for liquefied natural gas (LNG) deliveries to the Union, the Agency should collect all the LNG market data that are necessary to establish a daily LNG price assessment and an LNG benchmark. The LNG price assessment and the LNG benchmark should be established on the basis of all transactions pertaining to LNG deliveries to the Union. The Agency should be empowered to collect the relevant market data from all participants active in LNG deliveries to the Union, which should report the LNG market data to the Agency as close to real time as technologically possible, either after the conclusion of a transaction or after the posting of a bid or offer to enter into a transaction. The Agency's LNG price assessment should comprise the most complete dataset including transaction prices, bids and offer prices for LNG deliveries to the Union. The daily publication of that objective LNG price assessment, and of the spread established in comparison to other reference prices on the market in the form of an LNG benchmark, paves the way for its voluntary uptake by market participants as the reference price in their contracts and transactions. DOCUMENT: Regulation amending REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Delegation of Tasks and Responsibilities Between Regulatory Authorities
ID: 21
CONTENT:
The delegation of tasks and responsibilities can be an effective instrument to reduce duplication of tasks, foster cooperation and aims to reduce the burden imposed on market participants. Therefore, a clear legal basis should be provided for such delegation. National regulatory authorities should be able to delegate tasks and responsibilities to another national regulatory authority or to the Agency, with the delegates' prior consent. The national regulatory authorities should be able to introduce specific conditions and to limit the scope of the delegation to what is necessary for the effective supervision of cross-border market participants or groups. Delegations should be governed by the principle of allocating competence to the authority which is best placed to take action on the subject matter. The rules on the performance of the duties of national regulatory authorities and of the Agency should ensure that conflicts of interest are avoided as far as possible.

DOCUMENT: Regulation amending REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Administrative Fines and Enforcement Framework for Market Manipulation
ID: 22
CONTENT:
A uniform and stronger framework to prevent market manipulation and other breaches of Regulation (EU) No 1227/2011 in the Member States is necessary. In order to ensure the consistent application of administrative fines across the Member States for breaches of Regulation (EU) No 1227/2011, that Regulation should be amended to provide for a list of administrative fines and other administrative measures which should be available to the national regulatory authorities as well as for a list of criteria to determine the level of those administrative fines. In particular, the amount of administrative fines which can be imposed in a specific case should be able to reach the maximum level provided for in this Regulation. However, this Regulation does not limit Member States' ability to provide for lower administrative fines on a case-by-case basis. Penalties for breaches of Regulation (EU) No 1227/2011 should be proportionate, effective and dissuasive and should reflect the type of the breaches, taking into account the ne bis in idem principle. The adoption and publication of administrative fines should respect fundamental rights as laid down in the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union. Administrative fines and other administrative measures are complementary parts of an effective enforcement regime. A harmonised supervision of the wholesale energy markets requires a consistent approach among national regulatory authorities. In order to fulfil their tasks, it is necessary that the national regulatory authorities be provided with the appropriate resources.

ID: 23
CONTENT:
Where a market participant that is not resident or established in the Union is active within the Union, it should designate a representative in the Union. text:
DOCUMENT: Regulation amending REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Cross-Border Market Abuse Enforcement Challenges
ID: 24
CONTENT:
To date, the supervision and enforcement of activities under Regulation (EU) No 1227/2011 have been the responsibility of the Member States. Market abuse behaviour is increasingly cross-border in nature, often affecting several Member States. Enforcement action against cross-border cases of market abuse can present jurisdictional challenges relating to the identification of the national regulatory authority that would be best placed to conduct the investigation in question. Cases of market abuse involving multiple cross-border elements and market participants established in third countries are also particularly challenging from an enforcement perspective. The current supervisory framework is not appropriate for the desired level of market integration. The absence of a mechanism to ensure the best possible supervisory decisions for cross-border cases, where joint action by national regulatory authorities and the Agency currently requires complicated arrangements and where there is a patchwork of supervisory regimes must be addressed. There is a need to set up an efficient and effective supervisory and investigatory regime for those cases of market abuse which cannot, due to their Union wide features, be addressed by Member State action alone.

DOCUMENT: Regulation amending REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Agency Investigation Powers for Cross-Border Market Abuse
ID: 25
CONTENT:
The investigation of breaches of Regulation (EU) No 1227/2011 with a cross-border dimension should be carried out through a uniform process at Union level. Moreover, such investigations can be better conducted at Union level, as their impact expands beyond the territory of a single Member State. The complexity of cross-border cases and the need to ensure sufficient resources for such cases requires the involvement of the Agency, in particular in a more integrated wholesale energy market. Since the entry into force of Regulation (EU) No 1227/2011, the Agency has gained significant experience in monitoring and collecting relevant data on the wholesale energy markets in the Union to ensure their integrity and transparency. Building on that experience, the Agency should be empowered to carry out investigations to combat breaches of Regulation (EU) No 1227/2011, including by appointing an independent investigating officer within the Agency. The Agency should carry out such investigations in cooperation with the national regulatory authorities and other relevant authorities with the purpose of supporting and complementing their enforcement activities and taking into account the ne bis in idem principle. Moreover, in the context of an investigation conducted by the Agency, where necessary, relevant national regulatory authorities should cooperate amongst each other in assisting the Agency. In exercising its powers, the Agency should be able to give priority, if needed, to the cases with the most significant cross-border impact. To fulfil the new obligations assigned to it, in particular those relating to enhanced investigatory powers in cross-border cases, the Agency should have adequate resources, including the necessary personnel.

text:
DOCUMENT: Regulation amending REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Cross-Border Dimension Criteria and Bidding Zones
ID: 26
CONTENT:
A main criterion for determining whether a case has a cross-border dimension relates to the delivery of wholesale energy products in a certain number of Member States. However, for technical reasons, there are cases where it is not possible to identify the geographic location of delivery of wholesale energy products. For instance, when delivery of wholesale energy products takes place or is assumed to take place in a bidding zone which encompasses the territory, or part of the territory, of at least two Member States in the intraday and dayahead wholesale electricity markets, it is not possible to identify the precise place of that delivery within that zone. The same applies to delivery of wholesale energy products that takes place or is assumed to take place in gas balancing zones which encompass the territory, or part of the territory, of at least two Member States. To ensure that the Agency acts in genuine cross-border cases as opposed to cases that have only a national dimension, the delivery of wholesale energy products within a bidding or balancing zone that encompasses the territory of at least two Member States should be considered to be delivery in a single Member State. However, the national regulatory authorities concerned should maintain their right also to request the Agency's involvement in cases with a cross-border dimension pursuant to this Regulation, as well as their right to object pursuant to this Regulation.

DOCUMENT: Regulation amending REMIT.pdf
SECTION: On-Site Inspection Powers and Procedures
ID: 29
CONTENT:
The Agency is empowered to conduct on-site inspections by taking statements and issuing requests for information to persons subject to investigation where suspected breaches of Regulation (EU) No 1227/2011 have a clear cross-border dimension. Officials and authorized persons may enter business premises where business records could be kept and private premises of directors, managers or staff members. However, investigations of private premises must be subject to a reasoned decision by the Agency and prior authorization of a national judicial authority. The Agency should closely cooperate with relevant national regulatory authorities, which must provide necessary assistance. Officials may affix seals on business premises for the period necessary for inspection, not exceeding 72 hours except in duly substantiated cases. Officials may request any information relevant to the subject matter and purpose of the on-site inspection.

SECTION: Periodic Penalty Payments and Procedural Safeguards
ID: 30
CONTENT:
The Agency is empowered to impose periodic penalty payments to ensure compliance with its decisions regarding on-site inspections and requests for information in cross-border investigations. However, the Agency is not empowered to impose fines. Any periodic penalty payments must be proportionate, effective and dissuasive to ensure efficient cross-border investigations. Procedural safeguards and fundamental rights of persons subject to investigations must be fully respected. Agency actions must be proportionate and ensure due process and rights of defence. Confidentiality of information submitted by investigated persons must be safeguarded and exchanged in accordance with applicable Union data protection rules.

DOCUMENT: Regulation amending REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Investigation Reports and Follow-Up
ID: 31
CONTENT:
At the end of each investigation, the Agency must draw up an investigation report including its findings and all evidence on which findings are based. The report must be submitted to national regulatory authorities of concerned Member States, which must, without prejudice to their exclusive competence for determining whether a breach occurred, take necessary enforcement measures including imposition of fines in accordance with this Regulation and national law. National regulatory authorities must do their utmost to ensure appropriate follow-up of Agency investigation reports. The Agency must regularly inform the European Parliament and Council of its cross-border investigation activities by submitting summaries of investigation reports on a regular basis in aggregated and anonymized form, treated as confidential in accordance with Regulation (EC) No 1049/2001.

SECTION: Judicial Review and Fundamental Rights
ID: 32
CONTENT:
Any decisions adopted by the Agency under this Regulation are subject to review by the Court of Justice of the European Union, including decisions imposing periodic penalty payments. This Regulation is without prejudice to the competence of national courts or tribunals to review decisions adopted by competent national authorities, such as authorizations by national judicial authorities in on-site inspections or claims of irregularities under national enforcement rules. This Regulation respects fundamental rights and principles recognized by the Charter, including protection of personal data, freedom to conduct business, right to effective remedy and fair trial, and the right not to be tried or punished twice for the same offence. It must be interpreted and applied in accordance with these rights and principles.

ID: 33
CONTENT:
The Commission is delegated power to adopt acts amending this Regulation by aligning relevant definitions to ensure coherence with other Union law in financial services and energy fields, and updating definitions for future wholesale energy market developments. The Commission may supplement this Regulation by specifying means for IIPs and RRMs to comply with obligations, details concerning authorization withdrawal and orderly substitution processes, relevant procedural safeguards, and establishing minimum thresholds for identifying events likely to significantly affect wholesale energy product prices. The Commission must carry out appropriate consultations during preparatory work in accordance with the Interinstitutional Agreement of 13 April 2016 on Better Law-Making, ensuring equal participation with European Parliament and Council receiving documents simultaneously with Member States' experts. Implementing powers are conferred on the Commission to be exercised in accordance with Regulation (EU) No 182/2011.

SECTION: Subsidiarity and Proportionality Principles
ID: 34
CONTENT:
The objective of this Regulation is to improve the Union's protection against market manipulation on the wholesale energy market. This objective cannot be sufficiently achieved by Member States alone but can be better achieved at Union level, in accordance with the subsidiarity principle set out in Article 5 of the Treaty on European Union. In accordance with the proportionality principle, this Regulation does not go beyond what is necessary to achieve that objective.

CONTENT:

DOCUMENT: Regulation amending REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Inside Information Definition and Precise Nature Criteria
ID: 38
CONTENT:
Information conveyed by a market participant or persons acting on their behalf to a service provider relating to pending orders in wholesale energy products is considered inside information if it is of a precise nature and relates directly or indirectly to one or more wholesale energy products. Information is of a precise nature if it indicates a set of circumstances which exists or may reasonably be expected to come into existence, or an event which has occurred or may reasonably be expected to occur, and is specific enough to enable a conclusion about the possible effect on wholesale energy product prices. Information may be considered precise if it relates to a protracted process intended to bring about particular circumstances or events, including future ones, and intermediate steps connected with those processes. An intermediate step in a protracted process is inside information if it satisfies the criteria of inside information. Information is directly or indirectly related to a wholesale energy product if it has a possible effect on demand, supply, prices, or expectations thereof. Information that would significantly affect wholesale energy product prices if made public means information a reasonable market participant would likely use as part of their trading decision basis.

text:
DOCUMENT: Regulation amending REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Market Manipulation Definition and Prohibited Conduct
ID: 39
CONTENT:
Market manipulation means entering into transactions, issuing, modifying or withdrawing orders to trade, or engaging in other behavior relating to wholesale energy products that: (i) gives or is likely to give false or misleading signals as to supply, demand, or price; (ii) secures or is likely to secure the price of one or more wholesale energy products at an artificial level, unless the person establishes legitimate reasons and conformity with accepted market practices; or (iii) employs fictitious devices or other deception giving false or misleading signals. Market manipulation also includes disseminating information through media or other means giving false or misleading signals about supply, demand, or price, including rumors and false news, where the disseminating person knew or ought to have known the information was false or misleading. Dissemination for journalism or artistic expression is assessed considering freedom of press and expression rules, unless the person derives advantage or profits from dissemination or intends to mislead the market. Additionally, transmitting false or misleading information or providing false input regarding benchmarks, or engaging in behavior leading to benchmark manipulation, constitutes market manipulation. Market manipulation may designate conduct of legal persons or natural persons participating in decisions to carry out activities for the legal person.
