SECTION: Example: Commissioning of New Plants or Re-commissioning of Mothballed Power Plants
ID: 90
CONTENT:
The process leading to the commissioning of new plants or re-commissioning of mothballed power plants is a lengthy and complex process. Its major milestones (for example: management board approvals, regulatory approvals, licence granting, etc.) constitute intermediate steps in this process. Some facts generated by the intermediate steps leading to the commissioning or re-commissioning of a power plant would qualify as precise information under REMIT, as they constitute a set of circumstances which exist or may reasonably be expected to come into existence and impact the realistic prospect of energy being produced from a certain point in time onwards. In order to decide whether these facts qualify as inside information, the three other criteria also need to be met.

ID: 91
CONTENT:

CONTENT:

To qualify as inside information, the management board decision must meet three additional criteria covered in Subchapters 3.3.2 to 3.3.4, beyond the precise nature requirement under REMIT.

DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Information That Has Not Been Made Public
ID: 93
CONTENT:
Inside information is information that has not been shared with the public, creating information asymmetries between market participants. Effective disclosure to the public transforms non-public information into public information. Information is deemed public if made available by any party to an unspecified number of market participants. No distinction is made regarding who made the information public. Information must be made available to the entire public of market participants simultaneously, ensuring equal access. Publishing information only to selected market participants, such as via email or exclusive news boards, does not satisfy public disclosure requirements. Generally accessible electronic systems for information dissemination, qualifying as Inside Information Platforms, can satisfy this requirement.

DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Information Relating to Wholesale Energy Products
ID: 94
CONTENT:
Inside information must relate, directly or indirectly, to one or more wholesale energy products. Wholesale energy products are defined as: (a) contracts for electricity or natural gas supply with delivery in the Union; (b) derivatives relating to electricity or natural gas produced, traded or delivered in the Union; (c) contracts relating to transportation of electricity or natural gas in the Union; and (d) derivatives relating to transportation of electricity or natural gas in the Union. Information with possible effects on demand, supply, and/or prices of wholesale energy products, or on expectations thereof, is considered directly or indirectly related. If information is likely to have significant price effects on wholesale energy products, it is necessarily related to these products. NRAs need only assess the likelihood of significant price effects to establish whether information relates to wholesale energy products.

DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Likelihood of Significant Price Effect Assessment
ID: 95
CONTENT:
Inside information must be likely to have a significant effect on wholesale energy product prices if made public. No actual price effect is required; mere likelihood suffices. Market participants must perform case-by-case assessments considering anticipated effects in light of information nature and market specificities. Relevant factors include: market characteristics (size, timeframe, design, liquidity, participant types); event size; published supply or demand information; transmission facility, storage, or network constraint availability; time of day; non-regular event announcements; TSO system announcements; and other market variables (weather, CO2, fuel prices, geopolitical developments). Market participants should establish systematic frameworks with clear internal compliance rules adapted to their activities and information types. Assessments must be performed ex ante before publication. NRAs may use ex post information to verify presumptions but should not act against those drawing reasonable ex ante conclusions.

text:
DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Example 1: Unplanned Outage Status Update Assessment
ID: 97
CONTENT:
Market participant A (MP A) operating a power plant discovers unplanned maintenance on a 100 MW generation unit must be extended by 2 hours. With limited market liquidity, MP A assesses whether this information would likely have significant price effects. Relevant ex-ante factors include: intraday market openness with two hourly and eight 15-minute products affected; limited order book depth; limited event size (100 MWh for two hours); no other announced outages; limited cross-border capacity; normal working hours; no additional announcements; no relevant wind forecast changes; and day-ahead pricing as reference. Assessment conclusion: Based on limited order book depth, absent cross-border transmission capacity, and changed information from previous disclosure, a reasonable market participant would likely use this extension information in trading decisions, making it likely to have significant price effects, particularly for directly linked hourly and 15-minute products.

DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Information on Trading Plans and Strategies
ID: 101
CONTENT:
According to Recital 12 of REMIT, information regarding a market participant's own plans and strategies for trading should not be considered as inside information. Trading plans are defined as plans including a systematic method for evaluating the supply, demand, or price of wholesale energy products, determining the amount of risk that is or should be taken, and/or formulating short- and/or long-term investment targets that may guide the daily trading activity. The consequences of these targets, in terms of energy needs and resulting orders to trade, should be considered as being part of the trading plans and therefore not constituting information under REMIT. Trading strategies are a set of objective rules designating the conditions that must be met for one or more trade entries and exits to occur, including specifications for order entries with filters and/or triggers, as well as rules for trade exits and order types. However, even if the details of the trading strategy do not qualify as inside information under REMIT, the facts used to determine or change it can be inside information.

ID: 102
CONTENT:
Market participant A sends an order with the following details: Buy order, Initiator, Flexible Hour order type (can trade at any hour provided price and volume are matched), Fill and Float conditions (killed immediately after matching or stays in market if not filled), Active status (activated by system or participant and visible in active order book), Minimum execution volume of 1,500 MW, Price limit of 40.5 euro, and Good Till Cancelled duration (persists until user cancels or reaches system maximum duration). text:
DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Application of the Obligation to Disclose Inside Information - Introduction
ID: 104
CONTENT:
According to Article 4(1) of REMIT, market participants shall publicly disclose in an effective and timely manner inside information which they possess in respect of business or facilities which the market participant concerned, or its parent undertaking or related undertaking, owns or controls or for whose operational matters that market participant or undertaking is responsible, either in whole or in part. Such disclosure shall include information relevant to the capacity and use of facilities for production, storage, consumption or transmission of electricity or natural gas or related to the capacity and use of LNG facilities, including planned or unplanned unavailability of these facilities. The obligation to disclose inside information lies with the market participant according to Article 4(1) of REMIT and relates to inside information in respect of the market participant's own business or facilities, as well as to inside information of the market participant's parent undertaking or related undertaking.

text:
DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Scope of Disclosure Obligations and Related Undertakings
ID: 105
CONTENT:
The disclosure obligation is not only related to inside information in respect of business or facilities which the market participant or respective undertakings own(s) or control(s), but also in respect of business or facilities for whose operational matters the market participant or respective undertaking is responsible, either in whole or in part. The obligation to disclose inside information does not apply to a person or a market participant who possesses inside information in respect of another market participant's business or facilities, in so far as that owner of this inside information is not a parent or related undertaking. However, persons holding information in such circumstances will need to consider their compliance with Article 3 and in particular whether they hold such information as one of the persons listed in Article 3(2). The Agency encourages persons holding such information to promptly inform the relevant market participant(s) in order to promote effective and timely compliance with Article 4(1) of REMIT.

SECTION: Disclosure Obligations for Employees and Representatives
ID: 106
CONTENT:
Article 4(3) of REMIT extends the disclosure obligation of Article 4(1) to a person employed by, or acting on behalf of, a market participant when that person discloses inside information to any other person in the normal course of the exercise of their employment, profession or duties as referred to in Article 3(1)(b) of REMIT. In such a case, that market participant or person shall ensure simultaneous, complete and effective disclosure of that information. However, the disclosure obligation of Article 4(3) of REMIT does not apply if the person receiving the information has a duty of confidentiality, regardless of whether such duty derives from law, regulation, articles of association or contracts.

text:
DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Disclosure Mechanisms and Inside Information Platforms
ID: 107
CONTENT:
The transparency of the wholesale energy markets requires the disclosure of inside information in a manner that enables the dissemination of information to as wide a public as possible, granting easy and equal access to all users of this information. The Agency believes that, in order to achieve effective disclosure according to Article 4 of REMIT, the information shall be disclosed using a platform for the disclosure of inside information (Inside Information Platform or IIP), i.e. an electronic system for the delivery of information which allows multiple market participants to share information with the wide public and complies with the minimum quality requirements. Using Inside Information Platforms as the default disclosure mechanism is supported by the combined reading of Article 4(1) and Article 4(4) of REMIT.

Using Inside Information Platforms as the default disclosure mechanism is supported by: (a) This disclosure mechanism is indicated by Article 4(4) of REMIT, which states that publication of inside information in accordance with Regulation (EU) 2019/943 or (EC) No 715/2009, or guidelines and network codes adopted pursuant to those Regulations, constitutes simultaneous, complete and effective public disclosure. The transparency rules under these regulations stipulate publication on central information transparency platforms. (b) This disclosure mechanism promotes convergence with technical standards established under financial market legislation, in particular those established under Article 17 of MAR, as further specified in Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2016/1055. (c) The reduction in the number of publication channels leads to a significant reduction in complexity and effort for market participants to access and use information published according to Article 4 of REMIT.

ID: 109
CONTENT:
In order to facilitate compliance with the disclosure obligation, a list of Inside Information Platforms available in Europe for the disclosure of inside information on wholesale energy markets is published on the Agency's REMIT Portal, following an assessment of IIPs' compliance with quality requirements, requirements for the reporting of inside information to the Agency described in the REMIT Manual of Procedures on transaction data, fundamental data and inside information reporting (REMIT MoP) and the Guidance on the implementation of web feeds. text:
DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Additional Publication Methods and Market Participant Registration
ID: 110
CONTENT:
A simultaneous publication on the market participant's website or through social media may be used as an additional source for publication. However, it cannot replace the disclosure on Inside Information Platforms. In case additional means for publication are used, the market participant must ensure that the published information is identical to the one published on the Inside Information Platform. The publication of inside information on platforms facilitates access to information for all market participants and promotes the overall transparency of the market. Moreover, this solution decreases overall the technical and organisational burden for market participants. In the registration process according to Article 9(5) of REMIT, market participants possessing inside information are required to promptly provide and regularly update information on the place of publication of inside information. This information is made publicly available by the Agency as part of the European Register of Market Participants (CEREMP).

SECTION: Minimum Quality Requirements for Effective Disclosure of Inside Information
ID: 113
CONTENT:
The following minimum requirements shall be fulfilled by the Inside Information Platform in order to ensure an effective disclosure of inside information: inside information shall be disclosed to as wide a public as possible on a non-discriminatory basis and shall be accessible free of charge, simultaneously throughout the affected energy market(s); electronic means shall be used to ensure that the completeness, integrity and confidentiality of the information provided by the market participants is maintained during its transmission, reception, storage and processing to the platform; inside information shall be made publicly available in a way that must have the ability to actively distribute the information with the goal to reach the public at large and specific for the disclosure of inside information, allowing easy and fast access by the public.

text:
DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Platform Technical and Operational Requirements
ID: 114
CONTENT:
The platform shall facilitate active distribution of inside information by means of web feeds in a way that enables the Agency to collect and market participants to process these data efficiently, in line with the Guidance on the implementation of web feeds and the REMIT MoP published on the REMIT Portal. The filtering of information, including historical information, by relevant data categories should be possible in order to promote its efficient use, including in a downloadable format. Historical inside information, including any edited information, shall be kept available for the public for a period of at least 5 years after the termination of the corresponding event(s). Any history of prior publications regarding the same event shall be easily accessible and a functionality should be provided linking the previous publications to the new publication(s) in a comprehensible and easy-to-use manner.

DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Platform Reliability, Language, and Conflict of Interest Requirements
ID: 115
CONTENT:
Effective redundancy, backup and/or fallback solutions, as well as minimal delay of publication and unavailability of the service provided by a platform, shall be ensured. The information should either be published in the official language(s) of the relevant Member State and in English or in English only. Effective administrative arrangements shall be designed by the platform provider to prevent conflicts of interest with market participants. While market participants are responsible for the disclosure of inside information, the Agency understands that they do not have influence on the operation of platforms. Therefore, the Agency believes that market participants are not responsible for temporary technical problems of such platforms fulfilling the above-mentioned minimum quality requirements.

text:
DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Market Participant Responsibility and Backup Solutions
ID: 116
CONTENT:
If the information was transmitted to the platform in time and there were temporary technical problems, the market participant should therefore not be considered for having breached the obligation to disclose inside information. In such circumstances, market participants could also consider a backup solution, provided that it complies with same relevant minimum quality requirements listed above. In this case, they should provide information on the backup solution in the process of registration according to Article 9(5) of REMIT. If technical problems persist, however, market participants should consider using other platforms to comply with the disclosure obligation. Where disclosure is delayed in such circumstance, the market participant will need to consider its compliance with the prohibition in Article 3 prior to the information actually being disclosed to the market.

DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Content Requirements for Inside Information Publications
ID: 117
CONTENT:
Without prejudice to Article 1(2) of REMIT, the publication of inside information should be as concise and as specific as reasonably possible as well as precise and complete enough to allow a correct understanding of the underlying event(s) that might potentially affect the prices of wholesale energy products. Further to that inside information should be disclosed in a format that enhances the overall transparency and ensures a Union-wide level playing field for market participants. Each publication made in accordance with Article 4(1) of REMIT, in the form of Urgent Market Message – UMM, should include the information set, as described in the tables (respectively one for electricity, one for natural gas and one for other type of event/information) included in ANNEX VII of the REMIT MoP, as applicable.

DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Format, Disclaimers, and Prognosis Requirements
ID: 118
CONTENT:
The information has to be provided according to the explanatory rules documented in ANNEX VII of the REMIT MoP. All fields and allowed values listed in ANNEX VII of the REMIT MoP should be supported by the platform. Each publication should not include statements by company executives, any form of advertisement or any other irrelevant information. For the same reason, the Agency discourages the use of disclaimers. If disclaimers are used, they should be clearly separated from the main body. If the publication requires a prognosis, e.g. regarding the duration of an outage, the Agency understands that such prognosis contains an element of uncertainty. Therefore, the Agency believes that market participants fulfil their publication requirements if the prognosis is based on all available data and has been prepared with reasonable effort.

ID: 119
CONTENT:
If a prognosis changes over time, the publication should be updated accordingly as soon as the new information is available. The obligation to disclose inside information is without prejudice to the application of European Union competition law. It is the Agency's understanding that the disclosure of inside information in an incomplete or incorrect manner would be considered as a non-effective disclosure and thus be in breach of Article 4(1) of REMIT.

text:
DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Timely Disclosure of Inside Information - Regulated Information
ID: 120
CONTENT:
As regards the notion of timely disclosure of inside information, the Agency currently considers that if the inside information has to be published in accordance with Regulation (EU) 2019/943 and (EC) No 715/2009, including guidelines and network codes adopted pursuant to those Regulations, and Commission Regulation (EU) No 543/2013, the publishing according to these rules and regulations, including in aggregated form, is considered simultaneous, complete and effective public disclosure (Article 4(4) of REMIT). However, it has to be stressed that even if Article 4(4) of REMIT states that the publication of inside information, including in aggregated form, in accordance with the above-mentioned Regulations, constitutes simultaneous, complete and effective public disclosure, it does not necessarily constitute disclosure in a timely manner and the inside information has to be published, in any case, before trading in wholesale energy products to which that information relates, or recommending another person to trade in wholesale energy markets to which that information relates.

text:
DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Timely Disclosure of Inside Information - Non-Regulated Information
ID: 121
CONTENT:
If the inside information does not have to be made public in accordance with Regulation (EU) 2019/943 and (EC) No 715/2009 and Commission Regulation (EU) No 543/2013, the Agency currently considers that there is no reason for applying a different reasonable timeframe for the disclosure of information than stated in the above-mentioned Regulations. Such information should therefore normally be published as soon as possible, but at the latest within one hour if not otherwise specified in applicable rules and regulations. But in any case the inside information has to be published before trading in wholesale energy products to which that information relates or recommending another person to trade in wholesale energy markets to which that information relates. The Agency considers that market participants should develop a clear compliance plan towards real time or close to real time disclosure of inside information, beyond compliance with existing Third Package transparency obligations.

text:
DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Delayed Disclosure of Inside Information - Legal Framework
ID: 122
CONTENT:
According to Article 4(2) of REMIT, a market participant may exceptionally delay the public disclosure of inside information. According to Article 4(2): "A market participant may under its own responsibility exceptionally delay the public disclosure of inside information so as not to prejudice its legitimate interests provided that such omission is not likely to mislead the public and provided that the market participant is able to ensure the confidentiality of that information and does not make decisions relating to trading in wholesale energy products based upon that information. In such a situation the market participant shall without delay provide that information, together with a justification for the delay of the public disclosure, to the Agency and the relevant national regulatory authority having regard to Article 8(5)."

text:
DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Delayed Disclosure - Agency Role and Market Participant Obligations
ID: 123
CONTENT:
The decision to exceptionally delay the public disclosure of inside information in accordance with Article 4(2) is for market participants to make. It is not the role of the Agency or NRAs to pre-approve the application of Article 4(2) to a specific set of circumstances. In any instance where a market participant chooses to delay disclosure, it must ensure that such a delay is not likely to mislead the public, that it does not make trading decisions on that information and that the information remains confidential. As Article 4(2) requires that the market participant does not make trading decisions based on that inside information, the Agency underlines that the application of Article 4(2) cannot coincide with the application of Article 3(4)(b) of REMIT.

SECTION: Delayed Disclosure - Ex-Post Determination and Notification Format
ID: 124
CONTENT:
Whether a market participant rightly or falsely applied Article 4(2) can only be determined ex-post. As soon as the legitimate interests cease to exist, the market participant must disclose the inside information in accordance with Article 4(1). In order to assist those market participants who are subject to the obligation to report information on the delay of the public disclosure of inside information to the Agency and the NRA according to Article 4(2) of REMIT, the Agency has developed a standard notification format, based on the experience in financial markets, and recommends its adoption by all NRAs. The relevant electronic format is published on the Agency's website.

SECTION: Critical Infrastructure and Inside Information Disclosure
ID: 127
CONTENT:
Market participants holding inside information about critical infrastructure they own, control, or are responsible for can delay publication if the information constitutes 'sensitive critical infrastructure protection related information' as defined in Article 2(d) of Council Directive 2008/114/EC. This applies to facts about critical infrastructure which, if disclosed, could be used to plan disruption or destruction. However, this exemption does not apply to all inside information relating to critical infrastructure. If inside information does not constitute 'sensitive critical infrastructure protection related information', the obligation to publish remains.

text:
DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: REMIT Prohibition of Insider Trading - Introduction
ID: 128
CONTENT:
Article 3(1) of REMIT prohibits persons who possess inside information from: (i) using it for trading or trying to trade, (ii) disclosing it to any other person, or (iii) recommending or inducing trading based on it. This guidance explains the concept of insider trading as laid down in Article 3(1) of REMIT, describing its different forms and exploring relevant elements in its definition. The guidance includes examples relevant to wholesale energy markets and provides indicators to help NRAs identify potential insider trading, including both simple signals and complex practices combining different signals.

text:
DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Definition of Insider Trading - Three Forms
ID: 129
CONTENT:
Article 3(1) of REMIT defines three different forms of insider trading prohibition: (a) using inside information by acquiring, disposing of, or trying to acquire or dispose of wholesale energy products for one's own account or a third party's account, directly or indirectly; (b) disclosing that information to any other person unless disclosure is made in the normal course of employment, profession or duties; (c) recommending or inducing another person to acquire or dispose of wholesale energy products based on inside information. The first form includes two nuances: actual use of inside information to trade and attempted use of inside information to trade.

The first form includes two nuances: actual use of inside information to trade and attempted use of inside information to trade.

text:
DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: On-Market vs Off-Market Insider Trading Practices
ID: 130
CONTENT:
Only the first form of insider trading prohibition (Article 3(1)(a)) involves using inside information for trading or trying to trade, constituting an 'on-market' practice. The other two forms (Articles 3(1)(b) and 3(1)(c)) involve transmission of inside information or recommendations based on it, and are 'off-market' practices. On-market attempted forms include trying to acquire or dispose of wholesale energy products. On-market effect forms include acquiring or disposing of wholesale energy products. Off-market forms include disclosing inside information and recommending or inducing acquisition/disposal of wholesale energy products.

text:
DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Purpose and Unfair Advantage in Insider Trading
ID: 131
CONTENT:
The purpose of REMIT is to protect transparency and integrity of wholesale energy markets and ensure a level-playing field for market participants. Possession of inside information creates an unfair informational advantage and information asymmetries between market participants, undermining market transparency, integrity, and participant confidence. The unfair advantage from asymmetric knowledge does not need to materialize into financial benefit for the person involved to breach REMIT. NRAs need not determine whether transactions, disclosures, or recommendations ensured gains for any parties to qualify a practice as insider trading.

text:
DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Liability and Timing of Insider Trading Breach
ID: 132
CONTENT:
The prohibition on using inside information applies from the moment a legal or natural person comes into possession of such information. Liability for insider trading is established as soon as a person initiates trading, including placing an order based on inside information, tries to trade based on inside information, discloses inside information, or recommends/induces trading based on inside information. When assessing potential breaches of Article 3(1) of REMIT, NRAs should evaluate the person's compliance with obligations to publish inside information established in Article 4(1) of REMIT.

DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Freedom of Press and Expression - Misuse Prohibition
ID: 133
CONTENT:
Article 3(6) of REMIT recognizes freedom of press and freedom of expression in other media for dissemination of information for journalism or artistic expression purposes. However, misuse of this freedom is prohibited. Misuse consists of situations when: (i) the person derives undue advantage or profit from dissemination, or (ii) disclosure or dissemination is made with intention to mislead the market regarding supply, demand, or price of wholesale energy products. Proper use requires acting in good faith, with professionalism, and in accordance with press codes including verification processes for accuracy and credibility.

CONTENT:

SECTION: Insider Trading by Using Inside Information - Concept
ID: 135
CONTENT:
The first form of insider trading (Article 3(1)(a) of REMIT) consists of using inside information by acquiring or disposing of, or trying to acquire or dispose of, wholesale energy products for one's own account or a third party's account, directly or indirectly. This form encompasses four relevant concepts: (1) acquisition or disposal of wholesale energy product(s) or attempt thereof; (2) for one's own account or for a third party's account; (3) directly or indirectly; and (4) the information being related to wholesale energy products.

SECTION: Acquiring or Disposing of Wholesale Energy Products
ID: 136
CONTENT:
The concept of 'acquiring or disposing of' encompasses all types of actions related to orders and transactions or part of processes of issuing orders or entering into transactions in wholesale energy markets. This includes issuance of new orders, amendment/modification of existing orders, cancellation of orders, establishment of links or dependencies between orders, or any other action relating to entering into transactions or issuing orders. In certain circumstances requiring case-by-case assessment, this can include non-issuance of orders based on inside information.

SECTION: Hands-Off Approach and Insider Trading Compliance
ID: 137
CONTENT:
In light of REMIT's scope and objectives, natural or legal persons shall refrain from any amendment or selective withdrawal of any order(s) placed before having access to inside information (hands-off approach) to comply with the insider trading prohibition. This requirement applies regardless of whether the person(s) committed insider trading deliberately or recklessly, as the prohibition consists of purely material actions or absence of expected action resulting in use of inside information by acquiring or disposing of wholesale energy products.

SECTION: Proof Standards for Insider Trading Violations
ID: 138
CONTENT:
In assessing insider trading violations involving 'acquiring or disposing of' wholesale energy products, NRAs should prove use of inside information with either: (i) tangible evidence of possession of inside information chronologically preceding trading in the relevant wholesale energy product by the person(s) concerned, or (ii) in absence of tangible evidence, a set of precise and consistent pieces of evidence such as evidence of actions undertaken, absence of expected actions, absence of robust and well-documented controls of information flow processes, or absence of proper Chinese walls between the area possessing inside information and the trading area, establishing that only use of such information can explain their trading.

text:
DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Insider Trading Prohibition and Use of Inside Information
ID: 139
CONTENT:
A breach of the insider trading prohibition under Article 3(1)(a) of REMIT may be established irrespective of a transaction. Article 3(1)(a) refers explicitly to the use of inside information 'by acquiring or disposing of' a wholesale energy product or 'trying' to do so. Whenever a person in possession of inside information acquires or disposes of, or attempts to acquire or dispose of, for their own account or for the account of a third party, directly or indirectly, the wholesale energy product to which that information relates, it should be concluded that that person, unless otherwise proven, has used inside information. Such a person is therefore accountable for a breach of Article 3(1)(a) of REMIT. That presumption is without prejudice to the rights of the defence.

text:
DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: For One's Own Account or for the Account of a Third Party
ID: 140
CONTENT:
Article 3(1)(a) of REMIT establishes that acquisitions or disposals of wholesale energy products can be to the person's own account or to the account of third parties. This extends the scope of insider trading to situations where the person holding inside information uses third party accounts (i.e. the account from another natural or legal person) and to situations where the eventual beneficiary of the insider trading activity is not necessarily the person who holds the inside information and is using it by trading. In the context of trading in wholesale energy markets, the natural person using the information to acquire/dispose of wholesale energy products is often not doing so on their personal account, but rather on the account of the legal person (typically the legal account of their employer or of a related undertaking) on whose behalf they are acting. Some legal persons (mostly market participants) may also manage portfolios of other legal persons. The acquisition or disposal of a wholesale energy product for the account of a third party can also consist of an 'interposition' in the transaction, where the market participant acquires the wholesale energy product on behalf of its parent undertaking (or shareholder) or to fulfil obligations arising from the management agreement.

text:
DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Directly or Indirectly Acquiring or Disposing of Wholesale Energy Products
ID: 141
CONTENT:
Using inside information by acquiring or disposing of wholesale energy product(s) can be carried out either directly or indirectly. Direct acquisition/disposal of a wholesale energy product (or an attempt thereof) happens if the person possessing inside information acquires/disposes of a wholesale energy product itself (or attempts to do so). Indirect acquisition/disposal of a wholesale energy product (or an attempt thereof) happens when the person possessing inside information acquires/disposes of a wholesale energy product (or attempts to do so) through a third party (e.g. through a broker, a related undertaking, another market participant or another person). Indirect use can happen through a legal person's parent undertaking, where the order/transaction is performed by the parent undertaking (or shareholder) and the legal person does not have any statutory management powers over that entity. Indirect use can also happen through a market participant executing an order/transaction on their own account after being instructed to do so by a parent undertaking (or shareholder) that holds inside information.

Indirect use can happen through a legal person's parent undertaking, where the order/transaction is performed by the parent undertaking (or shareholder) and the legal person does not have any statutory management powers over that entity. text:
DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Wholesale Energy Products to Which Information Relates
ID: 142
CONTENT:
The definition of 'insider trading' in Article 3(1)(a) of REMIT requires that inside information is used to acquire or dispose of, directly or indirectly, the wholesale energy product to which that inside information relates. Inside information relates to the products that have at least part of the delivery during the time when events that constitute inside information take place (e.g. inside information on a one-hour outage could relate to the intraday product of this specific hour, while an outage of several weeks could relate to intraday, day-ahead, weekly, monthly, quarterly, and yearly forwards and futures). Inside information also relates to the products whose prospects on supply, demand and price are indirectly affected by the information (e.g. inside information on an unplanned one-hour outage could also relate to intraday products adjacent to this hour, as the information creates uncertainty about potential delays in resuming normal operation). Factors such as the size of events, the technology affected, and the reliability of a given power plant are relevant to establishing the scope of potential wholesale energy products to which that inside information relates.

text:
DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Example: Using Inside Information by Entering into Transactions - Lack of Timely Updates
ID: 143
CONTENT:
Situation: Market participant ('MP') A owns and operates a gas storage facility with a daily withdrawal capacity of 100 MWh. The storage facility is going through a planned two-week maintenance period without any possibility of withdrawing or injecting gas. MP A published this maintenance through an urgent market message ('UMM') on an inside information platform. Five days before the planned end of maintenance (D-5), MP A receives information that the maintenance is finished ahead of schedule and that withdrawal of natural gas will be possible as of the end of the day (at 24:00). MP A decides to withdraw the gas and sell it on the within-day market from D-4 onwards. MP A is aware that the liquidity in the within-day market of the bidding zone ('BZ') in which the storage facility is located ('BZ A') is rather low and therefore decides to sell the gas on the within-day market of BZ B, a larger neighbouring market. At D-5 18:00, MP A informs the TSO dispatch centre on the updated details of the storage operation schedule for D-5 from 24:00 onwards. The information is not made public, as the TSO is not required to publish it in D-5. From D-5 21:00 to 24:00, MP A acquires 100 MWh of within-day transmission capacity (hourly within-day products covering the following period: D-4 00:00 to D 00:00) from BZ A to B. At the same time, MP A sells its natural gas of 100 MWh in the within-day market of BZ B (hourly within-day products covering the following period: D-4 00:00 to D 00:00). At D-4 12:00, MP A updates the original UMM and informs the market of an earlier-than-expected finalisation of its maintenance from D-4 00:00 onwards. The market prices react downwardly.

text:
DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Assessment of Example: Insider Trading Breach
ID: 144
CONTENT:
MP A used inside information to acquire, directly for its own account, several wholesale energy products to which this information is related. The practice of MP A qualifies as insider trading and amounts to a breach of Article 3(1)(a) of REMIT, covering all elements foreseen in that provision. Inside information: At D-5 07:00 MP A received information on an early finalisation of maintenance of its storage facility. This information became precise at D-5 7:00, which is supported by the fact that at D-5 18:00 MP A informed the TSO dispatch centre on the updated operation schedule for D-4. Such information was precise, not public, related to the wholesale energy product, and likely to significantly affect the price of an intraday wholesale energy product. Acquiring or disposing of a wholesale energy product: MP A acquired transmission capacity from BZ A to B and sold its natural gas from the storage facility in BZ B, in the within-day markets. For its own account: MP A used its own account for these transactions. Directly or indirectly: MP A directly acquired the transmission capacity from BZ A to B and also directly sold the gas in the intraday market of BZ B. Wholesale energy products to which that information relates: This inside information is related to contracts for the supply of within-day gas transmission capacity from BZ A to B (also from BZ B to A) at least for hourly contracts between D-4 00:00 to D 00:00; contracts for the supply of day-ahead gas transmission capacity from BZ A to B (also from BZ B to A) at least for daily contracts between D-4 to D-1 (inclusive); contracts for the supply of natural gas within day on BZ B's and BZ A's for at least hourly contracts between D-4 00:00 to D 00:00; and contracts for the supply of natural gas day ahead on BZ B's and BZ A's for at least daily contracts between D-4 to D-1 (inclusive). This practice also represents a breach of the obligation to publish inside information under Article 4(1) of REMIT.

text:
DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Example: Using Inside Information by Trading - Front Running
ID: 145
CONTENT:
Situation: On 27 December, Market participant ('MP') A signed a new contract for the one-year supply of 100 MWh of baseload of electricity for the following year to an end consumer. MP A wants to cover half of this supply (50 MWh) by buying electricity in the wholesale energy market. MP A decides to acquire this amount through a PPAT, so it informs the PPAT that this represents a major shift on its activity and that all quantity should be procured in the next few minutes in order to naturally hedge its position (but without providing further details). Taking into consideration the existing market circumstances, the PPAT selected by MP A expects that the short time given for the execution of the transactions will lead to an increase in the market prices of the yearly product. This would not happen if the client had given a longer time span for execution. Prior to introducing the client's order, the PPAT introduces other buy orders for the yearly physical forward on their own account in order to buy at the best ask. Once these orders are executed, the PPAT introduces buy orders on behalf of MP A. This leads to a significant increase in the price of the yearly product, which results in other market participants improving their bids. At this point, the PPAT sold the electricity bought on their own account, securing a gain.

SECTION: Insider Trading: Using Inside Information to Acquire Wholesale Energy Products
ID: 147
CONTENT:
This form encompasses two relevant concepts: the disclosure of inside information to any other person, and the disclosure is not made in the normal course of the exercise of employment, profession or duties. The PPAT used inside information to acquire, for their own account, the wholesale energy product to which that information relates. The 'front running' carried out by the PPAT qualifies as insider trading and a breach of Article 3(1)(a) of REMIT. Inside information includes information on MP A's need to execute a buy order of 50 MWh in the yearly physical forward market in a short period of time. From the PPAT's perspective, this information is inside information related to MP A's activity, as it is precise, not public, related to a wholesale energy product, and likely to significantly affect the price of a wholesale energy product. The PPAT entered into a yearly contract for the supply of electricity where delivery is in the Union (yearly physical forward) and acquired electricity directly for their own account.

text:
DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Client Orders and Inside Information Responsibilities
ID: 148
CONTENT:
A client's order to trade sent to the PPAT is part of the client's own trading strategy and does not constitute information under REMIT from the client's perspective. However, it can qualify as inside information for the PPAT, as it is not part of the PPAT's own trading strategy but rather the strategy of their client. The PPAT is not the relevant Market Participant that has to publish such information, as Article 4(1) of REMIT requires that inside information is published only in respect of business or facilities which the market participant concerned owns or controls. When a client's order is based on inside information, the responsibility for the breach of insider trading under Article 3(1)(a) of REMIT lies with the client and not the PPAT. If the PPAT is aware that the client's order is based on inside information, the PPAT is required to comply with their obligations under Article 15 of REMIT and notify the relevant NRA about the suspicious order or transaction.

ID: 149
CONTENT:
The concept of disclosure under Article 3(1)(b) of REMIT should not be confused with the public disclosure of inside information laid down in Article 4(1) of REMIT. Article 3(1)(b) aims at forbidding the disclosure of inside information before it is published in an effective and timely manner as requested by Article 4(1). The concept of 'disclosing information' includes any inside information that was not yet disclosed under Article 4(1) of REMIT, using any form of disclosure (including formal or informal mechanisms) and any possible means of communication. This prohibition is applicable to disclosure to any other person, whether to a single or multiple persons. The qualifying element for a breach of Article 3(1)(b) REMIT is the absence of 'normality' in the disclosure. To establish a breach, it is not relevant whether anyone received inside information and used it for trading, since it is the disclosure itself that is forbidden.

SECTION: Proving Disclosure of Inside Information
ID: 150
CONTENT:
NRAs can prove the disclosure of inside information to any other person either with tangible evidence of communication(s) between the parties involved in the unlawful disclosure of information or, in the absence of such tangible evidence, with a set of precise and consistent pieces of evidence. Such evidence may include evidence on the links between the person owning inside information, the third party, and ownership of inside information by the third party, establishing that only an unlawful disclosure of inside information could have occurred.

SECTION: Normal Course of Employment, Profession or Duties Exemption
ID: 151
CONTENT:
Article 3(1)(b) of REMIT provides an exemption to the prohibition of disclosure of inside information to any other person. The disclosure of inside information to any other person is not considered insider trading if it is done in the normal course of the exercise of the employment, profession or duties of a legal or natural person. This is in line with the obligation to publish inside information defined in Article 4(1) REMIT, ensuring symmetry of information among all natural and legal persons active in the wholesale energy markets. The disclosure of inside information in the normal course of the exercise of employment relationship, profession or duties should be interpreted in a strict manner.

SECTION: Assessing Normal Course Disclosure
ID: 152
CONTENT:
When assessing whether disclosure occurred in the 'normal course', NRAs may take into consideration whether the disclosure followed a pre-defined workflow based on the 'need-to-know' principle, or was included in the contract governing the person's duties. Whenever information is disseminated pursuing a personal objective (i.e. a benefit to the natural person), it should always be concluded that the disclosure is not made in the normal course of the exercise of employment, profession or duties.

text:
DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Example: Insider Trading by Disclosing Inside Information - Power Plant Maintenance
ID: 153
CONTENT:
Situation: Power plant (PP) A with a production capacity of 700 MW is located in bidding zone B, which has a total of 5,000 MW installed capacity. The head of technical operations is responsible for PP A's planned maintenances. In a morning management meeting, the head updates the PP A director about a planned maintenance scheduled for the following year for a period of 4 months. This information has not been shared with anyone else before and the PP A's compliance officer will be requested to publish it at 15:00. One hour after the management meeting, the PP A's director attends the PP A's trade union meeting. During the lunch break, the PP A's director talks informally to the trade union representative, mentioning the maintenance plan for next year and a potential coincidence of this maintenance with their social activity.

DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Assessment: Power Plant Maintenance Disclosure Breach
ID: 154
CONTENT:
Disclosure of inside information from the PP A's director to the trade union representative was not realised in the normal course of the exercise of their employment relationship, profession or duties. Therefore, such disclosure represents an improper disclosure of inside information and amounts to a breach of Article 3(1)(b) of REMIT. Inside information: Information on the long-term maintenance meets the criteria of inside information (precise, not public, relates to the wholesale energy product and likely to affect the wholesale energy product prices). Disclosing information to any other person: The director fulfils the definition of person possessing inside information under Article 3(2)(a) of REMIT. The disclosure of inside information by the director to the trade union representative qualifies as disclosure of inside information to other person specified in Article 3(1)(b) of REMIT.

DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Insider Trading by Recommending or Inducing Trading on Inside Information
ID: 156
CONTENT:
The third form of insider trading (within the meaning of Article 3(1)(c) of REMIT) consists of 'recommending or inducing another person, on the basis of inside information, to acquire or dispose of wholesale energy products to which that information relates'. The term 'recommending or inducing' should be interpreted as encompassing any action undertaken by the holder of inside information in order to provide to another person (also called the 'tippee') one or more direct or indirect signals relevant for trading on one or more wholesale energy markets that are related to that inside information.

DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Requirements for Article 3(1)(c) Breach
ID: 157
CONTENT:
Article 3(1)(c) of REMIT does not require the transmission of inside information to another person, but solely the transmission of a signal on the trading of wholesale energy products. Article 3(1)(c) of REMIT does not require any action from the beneficiary of the recommendation, i.e. it is irrelevant whether the person that received the recommendation used that information for trading or did not trade at all. The fact that the holder of inside information transgressed their obligation to refrain from making any recommendation to acquire or dispose of a wholesale energy product is sufficient to constitute a breach of Article 3(1)(c) of REMIT.

DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Example: Insider Trading by Recommending Trading - Power Plant Maintenance
ID: 158
CONTENT:
Situation: Market participant (MP) A owns and operates five power plants with a combined capacity of 2,000 MW (each power plant has the production capacity of around 400 MW). The chief technology officer (CTO) of MP A is informed that a component of the turbine used in all their power plants is defective and must be replaced in the near future. The replacement, which is expected to take ten days, is not urgent but should be carried out in the next quarter. All power plants will need to have an early maintenance. Based on that knowledge, the CTO recommends to their friend, an energy trader at Company B, to buy electricity forwards for the next quarter as soon as possible.

SECTION: Indicators of Insider Trading Overview
ID: 161
CONTENT:
In order to identify potential insider trading under REMIT, NRAs shall take into account the non-exhaustive list of indicators included in Subchapters 5.3.1 and 5.3.2, which shall not necessarily be deemed, by themselves, to constitute insider trading. The list is organised into simple signals (e.g. relevant variables, actions, or diagnostic flags) and more complex types of practices that typically combine different signals.

text:
DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Possible Signals - Volume and Price Changes
ID: 162
CONTENT:
Relevant and/or sudden changes in the traded volumes of wholesale energy products before the publication or occurrence of a fact that qualifies as inside information can indicate insider trading. This can happen when transactions and/or orders to trade from a particular market participant or a set of market participants are concentrated in a short time span of the trading session before the publication or occurrence of inside information. Additionally, before information on an unplanned outage on a market participant's own assets or the assets it is operating is published, there is often a relevant volume of transactions and/or orders to trade from that market participant on the wholesale energy products whose prices may be affected by that information.

DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Possible Signals - Price Movements and Trading Behavior
ID: 163
CONTENT:
Relevant and/or sudden changes in the prices of wholesale energy products before the publication (e.g. through urgent market messages) or occurrence of inside information can indicate insider trading. This occurs when the speed or magnitude of the changes in prices cannot be explained by the existing information available to the market and market fundamentals. Changes in the trading behaviour of a market participant in a wholesale energy product before the publication or occurrence of inside information include exhibiting an unusual trading profile (e.g. a substantially larger market share on orders or trades on one side of the order book) in a related wholesale energy product.

SECTION: Possible Signals - Order Cancellations and Position Reversals
ID: 164
CONTENT:
Market participants may cancel or modify orders and/or trades in a short time span, which represent a significant proportion of their daily volume. This indicator gains even further relevance if the cancelled/modified orders are associated with significant changes in the price of a wholesale energy product. Additionally, reversals of positions in a short period can indicate insider trading, especially if the reversals represent a significant proportion of the volume of orders or transactions of the market participant in a wholesale energy product.

DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Possible Signals - Profit Changes and Compliance Breaches
ID: 165
CONTENT:
Potential profit increase or change for a market participant, as a result of the change of its position on specific wholesale energy products and/or on a financial instrument before the publication or occurrence of inside information, can indicate insider trading. The lack of compliance with other REMIT obligations on inside information is also an indication of the possibility of insider trading. This can be the case when a market participant is at least sporadically in breach of the obligations of Article 4 of REMIT by not disclosing information either effectively or in a timely manner.

SECTION: Misuse of Article 3(4)(b) Exemption
ID: 166
CONTENT:
Market participants may misuse the exemption of Article 3(4)(b) of REMIT in several ways: not being one of the types of market participants eligible for the use of the exemption; not using its own available assets to cover the immediate physical loss; issuing orders/entering into transactions that go well beyond the strict need to cover the immediate physical loss; or trading for its own account when also trading on behalf of the asset owner under the exemption. These practices indicate potential insider trading violations.

DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Front Running or Pre-positioning Practice
ID: 167
CONTENT:
Front running or pre-positioning is a type of practice where a person or an associated person ('agent') that executes an order to buy or sell a wholesale energy product has material, nonpublic market information concerning an imminent order/transaction in that wholesale energy product or a related wholesale energy product prior to when that information is made publicly available or otherwise becomes stale or obsolete. A typical example is when an agent (e.g. PPAT) receives their client's order that meets the criteria of inside information and then trades on their own account on the basis of this information. In order to be compliant with Article 3(1) of REMIT, the agent is expected not to use the knowledge of the client's order to trade on their own agent's account before executing the client's order.

text:
DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Front Running Indicators
ID: 168
CONTENT:
The combination of the following signals can point to front running: Time proximity between the agent and client's order - an agent's order entered shortly ahead of their client's order (potentially suggesting that the agent may have received the client's unexecuted order prior to placing their personal trade); Better agent order - an agent's order may be placed at a price which is the same or better than their client's order; Potential profit by the agent - Front running often ends with the reversal of the agent's initial order after the execution of the client's order by selling (resp. buying) at a higher (resp. lower) price than the initial order, although this is not a necessary condition for front-running; and Repetition - Recurrent front-running trades are more suspicious and less likely to be genuine coincidences.

text:
DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Double Printing Practice
ID: 169
CONTENT:
Double Printing is a type of practice that includes several trades being made when only one is necessary to execute the order. A market participant acting as an agent receives an instruction from their client to execute an order and uses this information to trade on their own behalf. The agent does not directly execute the order on the client's behalf, even though the situation on the market would allow it, but executes it on their own behalf and then executes additional trade(s) between themselves and the client so that the price difference is captured by the agent to the detriment of the client. Double-printing transactions are usually performed on a market place and can be detected through trades of similar price and/or quantity, where the agent acting as principal, buys (sells) from (to) another market participant and sells (buys) to (from) the client.

text:
DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Scope of Insider Trading Prohibition - Five Categories of Insiders
ID: 170
CONTENT:
According to Article 3(2) of REMIT, the prohibition of insider trading applies to five categories of natural and legal persons who possess inside information in relation to wholesale energy products. Such persons are known as 'insiders'. The five categories are: 1) members of the administrative, management or supervisory bodies of an undertaking; 2) natural or legal persons with holdings in the capital of an undertaking; 3) natural or legal persons with access to the information through the exercise of their employment, profession or duties; 4) natural or legal persons who have acquired such information through criminal activity; and 5) natural or legal persons who know, or ought to know, that it is inside information.

text:
DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Scope Comparison - Insider Trading vs Market Manipulation
ID: 171
CONTENT:
The concept of persons who possess inside information included in REMIT goes well beyond the one of market participants or natural persons acting on their behalf. In contrast, the prohibition of market manipulation under Article 5 of REMIT applies to any natural or legal person. Article 3(5) of REMIT explicitly acknowledges that where the person who possesses inside information is a legal person, the prohibitions laid down in Article 3(1) of REMIT shall also apply to the natural persons who take part in the decision to carry out the transaction for the account of the legal person concerned. This puts a particular responsibility on the traders acting on behalf of market participants, and invites market participants to have proper compliance measures in place to ensure an appropriate workflow for the inside information handled.

text:
DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Examples of Insiders - Administrative and Management Bodies
ID: 172
CONTENT:
Members of the administrative, management or supervisory bodies of an undertaking who can be insiders include: Chief executive officer or other members of the management of an undertaking who are exposed to facts that can qualify as inside information; Managers of the control centre of a TSO/DSO deciding on the rescheduling of planned outages; Procurement managers responsible for the purchase/service contracts of the critical parts of a power plant; and Members of the supervisory board who are exposed to facts that can qualify as inside information.

SECTION: Examples of Insiders - Shareholders and Capital Holders
ID: 173
CONTENT:
Persons with holdings in the capital of an undertaking who can be insiders include: Shareholders (natural or legal persons) of the market participant who may be informed about the company's non-public information; and The legal person which possesses information with respect to business or facilities which its parent undertaking or related undertaking owns or controls or for whose operational matters that legal person or undertaking is responsible, either in whole or in part.

SECTION: Examples of Insiders - Employment and Professional Access
ID: 174
CONTENT:
Persons with access to information through the exercise of their employment, profession or duties who can be insiders include: A market participant which possesses information with respect to businesses or facilities which it owns or controls or for whose operational matters that market participant or undertaking is responsible, either in whole or in part; A natural person, acting on behalf of the market participant, which possesses information with respect to businesses or facilities which the market participant, or its parent undertaking or related undertaking, owns or controls or for whose operational matters that market participant or undertaking is responsible, either in whole or in part; and Persons professionally arranging transactions introducing and/or executing orders in the wholesale energy markets on behalf of their clients.

SECTION: Examples of Insiders - Criminal Activity and Knowledge
ID: 175
CONTENT:
Persons who have acquired information through criminal activity who can be insiders include: IT hackers stealing information from the IT system of the market participant or the IT system of the PPAT used by the market participant; and Market participant competitors that may have had access to that information through industrial espionage. Persons who know, or ought to know, that it is inside information include: Administrative staff that deals with the administrative processes regarding power plant unavailability; and The spouse, partner or friend of an employee of the market participant which typically possesses information with respect to businesses.

text:
DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Responsibility of Natural and Legal Persons - Trader X Example
ID: 176
CONTENT:
Trader X works for market participant A (MP A), an electricity producer owning and operating several power plants. Trader X accidentally listens to a conversation of two operational workers discussing details of an unplanned outage of one of MP A's power plants. This information meets the criteria of inside information. Trader X, expecting that the price of electricity is likely to increase due to the circumstances that led to the unplanned outage, decides to buy electricity on the wholesale energy market on behalf of MP A and sell it later with a profit. Trader X, as a natural person, is in breach of Article 3(1)(a) of REMIT as they meet the criteria of a person who ought to know that the information qualifies as inside information. Furthermore, Article 3(5) of REMIT explicitly acknowledges that the prohibitions of insider trading in Article 3(1)(a) of REMIT shall also apply to natural persons who take part in the decision to carry out the transaction for the account of the legal person concerned.

SECTION: Legal Person Responsibility and Article 4(1) Breach
ID: 177
CONTENT:
MP A could also be responsible for the breach of Article 3(1)(a) of REMIT, as trader X is trading on its behalf based on inside information that is held by employees of MP A. MP A is also responsible for a potential breach of Article 4(1) of REMIT, as the inside information was not published effectively. This is demonstrated by the fact that certain details regarding the unplanned outage were not provided to the market but seem to be price-relevant based on the trader behaviour.

text:
DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Article 3(2)(e) REMIT - Extended Scope and Indirect Responsibility
ID: 178
CONTENT:
Article 3(2)(e) of REMIT extends the scope of the provision to persons who know, or ought to know, that some item of information is inside information. Through this provision, a special responsibility is laid down for legal or natural persons that may be more indirectly related to the processes that generate or manage inside information or that are in contact, for personal or professional reasons, with persons dealing with inside information and may be at some point in time exposed to such information. This significantly expands the scope of the application of the provision of insider trading. When applying Article 3(2)(e) of REMIT, NRAs should consider, on a case-by-case basis, what a person knows or should have known about the business of a legal/natural person in the circumstances of each case of potential insider trading. Furthermore, the NRAs should consider if, given the professional experience of the person concerned and the transaction concluded, the person concerned should have known that the information qualifies as inside information under REMIT.

ID: 179
CONTENT:
Articles 3(3) and 3(4) of REMIT provide exemptions from the application of the prohibition of insider trading. These exemptions are designed to ensure consistent understanding of the circumstances under which these exemptions may be applied by National Regulatory Authorities (NRAs).

text:
DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Exemption under Article 3(3) - Transmission System Operators
ID: 180
CONTENT:
Article 3(3) of REMIT provides that points (a) and (c) of paragraph 1 of Article 3 shall not apply to transmission system operators when purchasing electricity or natural gas in order to ensure the safe and secure operation of the system in accordance with their obligations under points (d) and (e) of Article 12 of Directive 2009/72/EC or points (a) and (c) of Article 13(1) of Directive 2009/73/EC. The exemption from Article 3(3) of REMIT only applies to points (a) and (c) of Article 3(1) of REMIT. Point (b) of Article 3(1) and the other provisions of Article 3 of REMIT remain applicable. Therefore, when purchasing electricity or natural gas in order to ensure the safe and secure operation of the system, TSOs shall be prohibited from disclosing inside information to any other person unless such disclosure is made in the normal course of the exercise of their employment, profession or duties.

text:
DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: TSO Exemption Application and Scope Limitations
ID: 181
CONTENT:
The exemption from Article 3(3) of REMIT should only apply to the TSOs when acting in line with their tasks under points (d) and (e) of Article 40(1) of Directive (EU) 2019/944 or points (a) and (c) of Article 13(1) of Directive 2009/73/EC, and not when performing other tasks laid down in the above-mentioned Directives. For example, under point (d) of Article 40(1) of Directive (EU) 2019/944, TSOs can purchase electricity in order to ensure a secure, reliable and efficient electricity system (ensuring the necessary ancillary services) without breaching the prohibition of insider trading under Article 3(1)(a) and (c) of REMIT. However, the sole purpose of these transactions must be the safe and secure operation of the system.

text:
DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: National Market Models and Case-by-Case Assessment
ID: 182
CONTENT:
The Agency is aware that the market models of some Member States provide for specific tasks for certain market participants, similar to those of TSOs as regards to their responsibility to ensure the safe and secure operation of the system. As a result, these market participants hold information which, alone or in aggregate, can constitute inside information. In the exercise of the duties in connection with these specific tasks, those market participants carry out transactions in the name and on behalf of one or more other market participants. While there is an explicit exemption from the prohibition of insider trading in Article 3(3) of REMIT for TSOs, given that their duties are defined by EU law and are as such similar in all Member States, national particularities cannot be subsumed under the exemption in Article 3(3) of REMIT. With respect to the possible differences in national market models and the legal design of principal-agent-relations in different Member States, any such particularity needs to be assessed by the competent national authorities on a case-by-case basis.

text:
DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Exemption under Article 3(4)(a) - Pre-existing Obligations
ID: 183
CONTENT:
According to Article 3(4)(a) of REMIT, the prohibitions of insider trading shall not apply to transactions conducted in the discharge of an obligation that has become due to acquire or dispose of wholesale energy products where that obligation results from an agreement concluded, or an order to trade placed, before the person concerned came into possession of inside information. The Agency acknowledges that this exemption also applies under MAR and especially to transactions in derivative contracts conducted in the discharge of such obligations. Since the exemption also applies to orders to trade placed before the person concerned came into possession of inside information, the Agency considers that the market participant is obliged to refrain from any amendment or selective withdrawal of the placed order related to this inside information ("hands-off approach") in order to comply with the prohibition of insider trading.

text:
DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Exemption under Article 3(4)(b) - Unplanned Outages and Physical Loss
ID: 184
CONTENT:
Article 3(4)(b) of REMIT provides an exemption for transactions entered into by electricity and natural gas producers, operators of natural gas storage facilities or operators of LNG import facilities the sole purpose of which is to cover the immediate physical loss resulting from unplanned outages, where not to do so would result in the market participant not being able to meet existing contractual obligations or where such action is undertaken in agreement with the transmission system operator(s) concerned in order to ensure safe and secure operation of the system. In such a situation, the relevant information relating to the transactions shall be reported to the Agency and the national regulatory authority. This reporting obligation is without prejudice to the obligation set out in Article 4(1).

text:
DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Article 3(4)(b) Exemption - Scope and Conditions
ID: 185
CONTENT:
Concerning the exemption in Article 3(4)(b) of REMIT, the Agency considers that since the exemption is limited in scope to the market participants mentioned therein, any unplanned outage under the exemption of Article 3(4)(b) may only relate to production, storage or LNG import facilities. It furthermore considers that the exemption may only be applied for unplanned outages, i.e. outages which are not ex ante known by the primary owner of the data, and that any physical loss needs to be caused immediately and solely by that unplanned outage. The aforementioned market participants can only use this exemption to enter into transactions to cover the immediate physical loss. Any further trading that goes beyond covering the immediate (i.e. within the day) physical loss does not fall under the scope of this exemption.

text:
DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Article 3(4)(b) Exemption - Two Applicable Instances
ID: 186
CONTENT:
The exemption in Article 3(4)(b) of REMIT may only be applied by the aforementioned market participants for transactions in the following two instances: (1) where not to do so would result in the market participant not being able to meet existing contractual obligations; or (2) where such action is undertaken in agreement with the TSO(s) concerned in order to ensure a safe and secure operation of the system. Regarding the first instance, the Agency considers that the referenced contractual obligations must exist ex ante of the immediate physical loss resulting from unplanned outages. The existing contractual obligations must relate to the relevant period of the unplanned outage. The Agency considers a market participant as "not being able" to meet such existing contractual obligations only for situations that would lead to actual contractual breaches and only if the market participant has no other own assets available to fulfil the obligation.

SECTION: Article 3(4)(b) Second Instance - TSO Agreement and Safe Operation
ID: 188
CONTENT:
As regards the second instance of exemption in Article 3(4)(b) of REMIT, the Agency considers that the criterion "to ensure the safe and secure operation of the system" may apply in cases when market participants are, following an agreement with the TSO, acting on their behalf so that TSOs can ensure the safe and secure operation of the system in line with their obligations laid down in Article 40(1)(d) and (e) of Directive (EU) 2019/944 and Article 13(1)(a) and (c) of Directive 2009/73/EC. Under such circumstances, market participants may conduct transactions without breaching insider trading prohibitions when acting under TSO agreement for system security purposes.

ID: 189
CONTENT:
According to Article 3(4)(c) of REMIT, the prohibitions of insider trading shall not apply to market participants acting under national emergency rules, where national authorities have intervened in order to secure the supply of electricity or natural gas and market mechanisms have been suspended in a Member State or parts thereof. In this case the authority competent for emergency planning shall ensure publication in accordance with Article 4.

DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: TSO Market Participant Exemptions and Ancillary Services
ID: 190
CONTENT:
Market participant transactions acting on behalf of TSOs must have the sole purpose of ensuring safe and secure system operation. This exemption applies only when market participants act under specific agreement with TSOs at ancillary services markets, excluding all other wholesale energy markets. The exemption in Article 3(4)(b) may only be applied for the duration when the market participant cannot meet existing contractual obligations or when action is undertaken in agreement with transmission system operators to ensure safe and secure operation. If a market participant uses this exemption, relevant transaction information must be reported to the Agency and NRA as soon as possible. The Agency provides a secure Notification Platform at https://www.acer-remit.eu/np/home for simultaneous notification to both the Agency and relevant national regulatory authorities.

text:
DOCUMENT: 6th Edition ACER Guidance REMIT.pdf
SECTION: Emergency State Exemptions and Inside Information
ID: 191
CONTENT:
The exemption from Article 3(4)(c) of REMIT should only be used when an official state of emergency is declared by the competent authority of a Member State to secure electricity or natural gas supply, and market mechanisms have been suspended. The authority competent for emergency planning must ensure publication of inside information in accordance with Article 4(1) of REMIT. Market participants required by national emergency rules to enter into transactions while in possession of inside information will not breach Article 3 of REMIT. Situations for which remedial actions or contractual arrangements exist are not considered as leading to actual contractual breach. Becoming imbalanced due to unplanned outages is not considered a contractual breach as such.
